Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI paper with whole-brain group-level results (meets I5, I8, I10, I11), it does NOT meet key topical inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. The fMRI task is a placebo analgesia paradigm using thermal pain stimuli and expectancy manipulation, not an instructed emotion-regulation task with visual emotional stimuli. The independent cognitive reappraisal (CRA) lab task using visual images was performed outside the scanner and not used as an in-scanner regulation instruction; there is no within-fMRI contrast of an instructed regulation condition (e.g. reappraise > look) nor any visual-emotion stimulus regulation in the scanner. Therefore inclusion criteria I6, I7 and I9 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (instructed to reappraise vs view/maintain) using visual stimuli (negative and neutral pictures). It reports within-task regulation contrasts (reappraise > view; regulation×time interactions) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI peak coordinates and cluster statistics, alongside ROI results. The sample includes BPD patients and healthy controls with separate group results and responder/nonresponder analyses. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and supplemental material is not required to verify core criteria. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs an explicit emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) and compares it with a placebo and passive viewing. Emotional stimuli are visual (disgust images/IAPS), the sample is healthy adults (female), and the paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g. Reappraisal (Disgust>Neutral), Passive Viewing (Disgust>Neutral)) and whole-brain group-level analyses (voxelwise SPM results with FWE correction). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (I5, I6). Stimuli were visual IAPS pictures (static images) (I7). The sample includes clinical groups (BD, SZ) and healthy controls with results reported separately (I8). The analyses include within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraise > attend-negative; attend-negative > attend-neutral) (I9). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses were performed (3dMVM in AFNI) with cluster correction and reported cluster results (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is empirical with original fMRI data (not E3), reports whole-brain results (not only ROI; not E4), is not only connectivity/resting-state (not E5), includes within-task effects (not E6), and is not an empathy/perspective task without regulation instruction (not E7). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This paper reports a task-based fMRI study (Study 2) using an instructed cognitive reappraisal task (regulate vs experience vs observe) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). It includes adults from a clinical (gambling disorder patients) and healthy control groups and provides within-task contrasts (‘regulate’ > ‘experience’, ‘experience’ > ‘observe’) and within-group activation maps. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak MNI coordinates (e.g. x = -60, y = 20, Z = 32) and cluster thresholds, meeting whole-brain reporting criteria. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Study 2 reports a task-based fMRI experiment using instructed cognitive reappraisal ("CHANGE" vs "LOOK") during presentation of visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (look negative > look neutral; decrease negative > look negative) and group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates reported (Table 5). Participant groups (DSH and depression control) are reported separately. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus all required inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI study using instructed affect-labeling (an implicit emotion-regulation manipulation) and an affect-matching (unregulated viewing) task with visual stimuli (photographs of emotional faces). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (affect label > gender label) and viewing (affect match > shape match). Participants include clinical (SP subgroups) and healthy control groups with group-level SPM analyses normalized to standard space; peak coordinates and whole-brain main effects are reported (supplementary table). The methods, results, and discussion are present and complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal and distraction) while presenting visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (reappraisal vs view; distraction vs view; emotion vs neutral) and describes group-level analyses. The methods state that results were thresholded and that results significant at whole-brain FWE-corrected P<0.05 are reported, and the paper describes peak activations and connectivity differences across groups; coordinates are likely provided in tables/figures/supplementary materials per the journal format. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only results; within-task effects are reported). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete for screening.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructed participants to regulate emotion (increase vs. attend vs. decrease) using cognitive reappraisal-style strategies while viewing visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts (increase>attend, decrease>attend) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected clusters and coordinates (tables/figures). Sample characteristics are acceptable. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (explicit emotion regulation) while participants view visual stimuli (negative images). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraisal vs. Maintain and Reappraisal vs. Fixation), provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and cluster-correction thresholds, and includes ROI analyses for the amygdala. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I5–I11) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli (faces) and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain analyses (satisfies I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11). However, it does NOT instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraise/down-regulate/up-regulate/acceptance instruction); participants performed an emotion-identification/ignore-word interference task rather than an instructed regulation task. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation strategy) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text is complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (Reappraise vs Maintain) using visual stimuli (IAPS negative scenes; faces). The sample is healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Reappraise>Maintain) and other within-task contrasts (Surprise>Neutral, Fear>Neutral), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and peak coordinates (ROI coordinates and cluster results described). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs a cognitive reappraisal strategy (distancing) and contrasts distance vs permit conditions. Stimuli are visual (abstract cues and targets in a monetary incentive delay task) that elicit reward-related emotional responses; regulation is instructed during anticipation (expectation) and outcome periods. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Distance > Permit and related interactions), provides group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard MNI space (whole-brain/ROI analyses reported), and the full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met: this is empirical, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, and reports whole-brain voxelwise results. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which participants were explicitly instructed to apply emotion-regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal, suppression, up-regulation) while viewing visual stimuli (static high-calorie food images). The manuscript reports within-subject contrasts comparing regulation conditions (e.g., suppression vs. reappraisal, up-regulation vs. suppression) and describes a group-level, whole-brain RFX ANOVA with corrected F-map and identified fROIs in standard space. The sample (healthy adult women) is eligible. Reporting of whole-brain results and task contrasts satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion requirements. Full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present and sufficient for screening. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion-regulation (cognitive reappraisal) paradigm with visual picture stimuli. The paper reports within-task contrasts of interest (Regulate > Maintain and Maintain > Observe), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space, and provides results for both an obese patient group and healthy controls. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-visual stimuli, non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This full-text meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal variants (self-detach/self-immerse) (I6). Emotional stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). The sample includes clinical (MDD) and healthy control groups with results reported for both (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., detach > attend, immerse > attend) and within-group effects (I9). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described with reported peak coordinates in standard space (e.g., left IFG at -48,20,-4) and cluster correction (I10), and reporting in text/tables meets I11. No exclusion criteria are met: the study includes whole-brain task activation maps (not only ROIs or connectivity), includes within-group task effects, and is empirical. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs cognitive reappraisal of visual (IAPS) images and reports within-task contrasts and behavioral validation; however, the full text reports primarily ROI and seed-based (gPPI) connectivity analyses (L amygdala seed → R IFG) and does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation map (peak coordinates for a reappraise>watch type contrast) in the main article. The paper focuses on PPI connectivity and ROI-extracted beta coupling estimates, and refers to prior work and Supplement for broader results. Because the review requires at least one whole-brain task-evoked statistical map, this paper meets exclusion criterion E5 (only seed-based/ connectivity analyses reported without a whole-brain task activation map) and therefore must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (whole-brain evidence).

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed participants to perform an emotion-labeling task (affect labeling), which constitutes an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (I6). The emotional stimuli were visual (faces) (I7). The sample is a nonclinical adult sample reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (emotion label > gender label) and an unregulated viewing contrast (observe > fixation) (I9). Group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates are reported (I10) and results are presented in text/tables/figures (I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be included.

Exclusion reason: E4 applies — the study reports amygdala task activation using small-volume correction (ROI/SVC) and does not report a whole-brain task-evoked group activation map for the emotion contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (eligible sample: healthy adult participants), I9 (reports a within-task contrast: sad vs neutral). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy — participants performed autobiographical memory recall, not reappraisal/acceptance or other instructed regulation), I7 (stimuli are script-driven autobiographical recall accompanied by music, not visual emotional stimuli such as pictures or film), I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation map reported; primary activation was tested with SVC). Full text appears complete: fulltext_incomplete=false.

This report describes a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion-regulation paradigm (participants instructed to ignore emotional face distracters and focus on an n-back task), employing visual emotional stimuli (faces). It reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., 2-back + distracters > 2-back + no-distracters) and group-level task-evoked analyses (behavioral and BOLD activation results, ROI and whole-brain activity descriptions), and includes voxelwise group comparisons and PPI analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not only ROI/connectivity-only; within-task effects are reported). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (detach/experience) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Positive-Experience > Positive-Regulate; Negative-Regulate > Negative-Experience), trial-by-trial parametric analyses, and a group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis with MNI coordinates and cluster correction (tables/figures). Sample includes younger and older adults. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, sufficient for screening. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This study meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation — cognitive reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS images and face photographs), I8 (clinical sample qualifies), and I9 (reports within-task contrasts such as Reappraise > Maintain and Look contrasts). However, it does NOT provide a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or peak coordinates; analyses are ROI-based using AAL masks and the authors state no conclusions can be made at the whole-brain level. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports ONLY ROI results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal and suppression) during presentation of visual IAPS pictures, with training and in-scanner regulation. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > attend negative) and unregulated viewing contrasts, includes healthy controls reported separately alongside patients and siblings, and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses in SPM with cluster-level correction. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full-text provides a complete task-based fMRI study in which participants (AUD sample) performed instructed emotion-regulation tasks using visual stimuli (IAPS and alcohol/food images). The paper reports within-task contrasts for regulation (REAPPRAISE-Negative > LOOK-Negative; LATER > NOW) and whole-brain group-level activation maps with peak coordinates and cluster correction, plus tables/figures. All inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. The ER task directly matches the meta-analysis objective (regulated vs. unregulated viewing of visual emotional stimuli).

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS) and reports whole-brain task activation and emotion contrasts, but it does NOT instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy. The affective Stroop requires counting numerosity while emotional images act as distractors; participants were not instructed to reappraise, accept, distance, or otherwise regulate their emotional responses. Thus, inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation task) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task emotion contrasts/unregulated viewing), I10 (whole-brain group-level analyses with coordinates), I11 (results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. Meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual static image stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), and I11 (coordinates and results clearly described). Does NOT meet I6: participants were instructed simply to view/fixate the pictures (no instructed emotion regulation strategy such as reappraisal, distancing, or acceptance). Consequently it also fails I9: there is no within-task contrast explicitly indexing an instructed emotion-regulation condition (e.g., “reappraise > look”); reported contrasts compare contextual image conditions (religious vs non-religious) but do not reflect an instructed regulation manipulation. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study should be excluded for failing required inclusion criteria I6 and I9.

The paper is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (reinterpretation) to down-regulate negative emotion (meets I5 and I6). Stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). Sample is healthy adults (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise > Negative and Negative > Reappraise) (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported with FDR correction and coordinates/tables/figures (I10,I11). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion; no exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to up-regulate and down-regulate emotional responses during viewing of visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts (‘increase’ vs ‘attend’ for positive pictures; ‘decrease’ vs ‘attend’ for negative pictures) and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (cluster-corrected, coordinates reported in tables/figures) as well as ROI analyses. The sample is adult and reported group-level task activation maps. The methods, results and discussion are present in full. All predefined inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: the fMRI task did not instruct participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy (participants were instructed only to watch pictures while receiving thermal stimuli). The paper is a task-based fMRI study (I5), uses visual stimuli (I7), includes clinical and control samples (I8), and reports within-task contrasts/unregulated viewing contrasts (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal of appetitive visual stimuli (personally craved food images) and compares regulated and unregulated viewing. The task is a within-subjects fMRI craving-regulation paradigm (look vs regulate) with a choice manipulation; behavioral and neural contrasts (e.g., regulate > look, look > regulate, yes > no) are reported. Analyses include second-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects models using SPM/DARTEL with cluster correction and reported MNI peak coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not non-empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task contrasts, and is not an empathy/perspective-taking-only design). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion-regulation task (affect labeling: Label > Observe contrasts) with visual stimuli (faces). The paper reports within-task contrasts for negative and positive emotion regulation (NegLabel > NegObserve), conducts whole-brain voxelwise analyses (PPI whole-brain regressions and whole-brain activation regressions) with cluster correction and reports cluster results/coordinates (tables/figures), and includes an eligible sample (adolescent participants). Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (distancing, a form of cognitive reappraisal) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and Emopics images). The sample includes anorexia nervosa patients and matched healthy controls with group-level results reported separately. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., positive watch > positive distance, positive watch > neutral) and explicitly states that whole-brain analyses were performed and corrected (results reported in main/supplementary tables and figures). All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply (e.g., the study does not report only ROI/small-volume results nor only connectivity analyses). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is a randomized, placebo-controlled, task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (distraction vs. passive viewing) using visual IAPS pictures, reports within-task contrasts (distract-negative > attend-negative; attend-negative > attend-neutral), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI peak coordinates and statistical maps. Both PTSD patients and trauma-exposed controls are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply: the paper is empirical, reports whole-brain activation maps (not ROI-only), includes within-task effects, and is not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation instruction. Full text appears complete.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (face images) with group-level whole-brain analyses and reported peak coordinates, it does not test an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (criterion I6). The task is affect labeling (label the emotion) rather than an instruction to regulate (e.g., reappraise, accept, distance, or otherwise up-/down-regulate emotion). The main reported contrast (affect label > gender label) is not an instructed regulation > look contrast nor a passive viewing (emotion > baseline) contrast as specified in I9. Therefore it fails the key eligibility requirements for this review (I6 and I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I9. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly investigates instructed cognitive control over emotional/ social-action tendencies using an approach-avoidance (AA) task. The AA task requires participants to override automatic emotional action tendencies (affect-incongruent vs affect-congruent), which constitutes an instructed emotion-regulation/cognitive-control strategy. Emotional stimuli are visual (faces). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (incongruent > congruent) and links these to stress responsivity. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed and reported (with peak coordinates and SVC ROI results), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The full text (background, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

All inclusion criteria are met: This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed cognitive reappraisal (downregulate negative images; I6) using visual stimuli (IAPS static images; I7). The sample is healthy young adult females (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation and viewing (downregulate negative > attend negative; attend negative > attend neutral; I9). Group-level, whole-brain second-level analyses were conducted and t-maps/con images are provided (I10), and whole-brain results/coordinates are clearly described and included in supporting information (I11). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

EXCLUDED because the study reports only resting-state seed-based connectivity analyses (amygdala RSFC) and does not include any task-based fMRI or task-evoked contrasts. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (only seed-based connectivity/resting-state analyses with no whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample qualifies: methamphetamine-dependent adults). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation task), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli presented), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrast), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map). Full text appears complete. Thus the study does not address the review objective of task-based emotion regulation or viewing and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to regulate affect (up-regulate by “thinking happy thoughts” and down-regulate by “relaxing”), reports within-task regulation contrasts (up vs down), includes a suitable sample (children/adolescents), and provides group-level whole-brain analyses (see main text and supplementary Table S4/Fig S2). However, the experimental regulation was directed at internallygenerated affect via neurofeedback rather than regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli: the neurofeedback task did not present emotional visual stimuli during the regulation blocks (the visual faces were used only in the localiser), so the study does not meet the review’s requirement that the regulated stimuli be visual (I7). The meta-analysis objective specifically targets studies where participants regulate an emotional response to visual stimuli (or view them without regulating). Therefore, despite meeting several inclusion criteria, failure to meet I7 means exclusion.

The article reports an original task-based fMRI experiment using an instructed emotion-regulation task (explicit reappraisal ‘regulate’ vs ‘watch’), with visual emotional stimuli (30s film/video clips). The sample spans ages 23–88 (population-derived cohort). Analyses include within-task contrasts (e.g., negative regulate > negative watch; positive watch > neutral) and both ROI and whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (whole-brain results thresholded at p<0.05 FWE), with reported task-evoked activations. The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (only ROI results, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study with healthy adult participants using visual stimuli (offers and written messages), reporting within-task contrasts (e.g., unfair > fair) and whole-brain group-level analyses with coordinates. However, it does not meet the critical requirement that an emotion regulation strategy was instructed: participants performed an anger-infused Ultimatum Game without instructions to up- or down-regulate their emotions (implicit/automatic regulation only). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 and must be excluded from the review.

Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (within-task contrasts such as unfair > fair), I10 (whole-brain group-level analysis), I11 (reporting coordinates/tables). 
Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy).
Exclusion IDs met: None ([])

Excluded because the report presents task-based seed/PPI connectivity and ROI-based connectivity analyses without reporting any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or peak coordinates. This violates exclusion criterion E5. The study does meet several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (explicit instructed emotion regulation: reappraisal and acceptance), I7 (visual stimuli: emotional faces and video clips), I8 (clinical sample with SAD), and I9 (within-task contrasts such as affect label > gender label, reappraisal > passive viewing, acceptance > passive viewing). However, it does NOT meet I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates is reported). The full text appears complete. Confidence in this decision is high.

This study is a resting-state fMRI seed-based connectivity study using an acute tryptophan depletion challenge; it does not include any task-based emotion regulation paradigm or visual emotional stimuli. Exclusion criteria: E5 applies (reports ONLY resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses without any task activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample description qualifies). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not task-based fMRI), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli task), I9 (no within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked group-level activation map). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper must be excluded from this meta-analysis focused on task-based emotion regulation fMRI.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly addresses the review objective: participants received instructed emotion-regulation strategies (goal intentions vs implementation intentions) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (regulate > attend, attend > regulate), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (flexible factorial, reported activations, coordinate conversions), ROI and connectivity analyses, and behavioral and physiological measures. Sample is healthy adults and the full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria listed below.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs participants to regulate emotional responding (upregulate left amygdala during a happy memory induction; I6), includes an eligible sample (MDD patients; I8), reports within-task contrasts (Happy Memories vs Rest/Count; I9), and provides whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses and coordinates (PPI and group maps; I10). However, the regulated emotional stimuli are internally generated autobiographical memories rather than externally presented visual emotional stimuli (no IAPS/images/film/video stimuli), so it does not meet I7 (visual emotional stimuli). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli).

This full text clearly meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs emotion regulation strategies (increase/decrease via cognitive reappraisal/distancing) during the task (I6); stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7); sample includes clinical groups and healthy controls with results reported separately (I8); analyses report within-task contrasts (increase>maintain, decrease>maintain) (I9); group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster-level correction and peak coordinates (I10); results are presented in text/tables with coordinates (I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study reports whole-brain task activation maps (not only ROI or connectivity) and includes within-group task effects. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the emotional stimuli were word stimuli (rejection-themed words), which do not meet the review's stimuli inclusion (I7 excludes studies whose stimuli are word/sentence-based). Additionally, the task did not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met); though the study reports unregulated viewing contrasts (rejection > neutral) and thus meets the unregulated- viewing aspect (I9), other required criteria (I5, I8, I9, I10, I11) are satisfied. Whole-brain task-based fMRI was performed and reported, participants are an eligible sample (children), and within-task contrasts and whole-brain results are provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) were triggered. Therefore the study is ineligible due to failure to meet I7 (stimuli) and I6 (no instructed regulation).

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) with an emotional picture-processing task and explicit contrasts comparing negative, positive, and neutral conditions. Although participants were not instructed to apply an emotion-regulation strategy, the study reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., negative expected pictures vs neutral/positive) at the group level and provides whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses with reported significant clusters and coordinates. The sample includes a patient group (Takotsubo) and matched healthy controls reported separately. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion, and whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for studies that examine viewing (unregulated) of visual emotional stimuli and provides whole-brain task activation results suitable for the meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation (engagement vs. distraction) with whole-brain group analyses and within-task contrasts, but the emotional stimuli are auditory (audiotaped stories) rather than visual images or videos. This violates inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli must be VISUAL). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded on the basis of not meeting I7.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5 met) with an eligible sample (I8 met). It reports within-task emotion contrasts (unpleasant > neutral; pleasant > neutral) so unregulated viewing contrasts are available (I9 met) and it provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with tabulated results (I10 and I11 met). However, the study does NOT instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met) and the emotional stimuli are words (emotion-word Stroop), which the protocol excludes (I7 not met: the review excludes studies whose stimuli are word/sentence-based rather than visual images/films). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Because not all inclusion criteria are satisfied (specifically I6 and I7), the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive distraction (0-back vs 2-back) during anticipation of negative vs neutral IAPS pictures, qualifying as an instructed antecedent-focused emotion-regulation strategy (attentional deployment/cognitive control). Stimuli were visual (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts addressing regulation effects (e.g. interaction of valence and cognitive load; negative (0-back>2-back) > neutral (0-back>2-back)) and behavioral correlations, all from group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard space (MNI), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Sample (healthy adult females) is acceptable. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study uses a task (threat vs. safe cues) and reports ROI-based analyses of percent signal change during handholding conditions; however it does not meet critical inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (the report uses an ROI-based approach and extracts parameter estimates from predefined ROIs rather than presenting a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation map with peak coordinates). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: threat/safety cues were presented visually), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (within-task contrast reported: threat > safe). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as cognitive reappraisal or other instructed regulation—regulation here is social/supportive handholding, not an instructed cognitive/regulation task), I10 (no clearly reported whole-brain group voxelwise task-activation maps with peak coordinates). Full text appears complete.

This study is EXCLUDED because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance). Instead, the task required attending to and classifying visual stimuli (face/scene valence), probing implicit emotion regulation. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: faces and scenes), I8 (sample includes adolescents), I9 (reports within-task contrasts/unregulated viewing contrasts such as threatening > neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and cluster correction), and I11 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E7 not applicable). Because at least one required inclusion criterion (I6) is not satisfied, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (partner facial expressions), reporting unregulated viewing contrasts (partner negative > partner neutral) and group-level whole-brain results with coordinates, it does NOT meet inclusion criterion I6: there was no instruction to regulate emotion (participants were explicitly not instructed to regulate). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation with visual emotional stimuli and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain peak coordinates, but it does NOT instruct participants to use an explicit emotion-regulation strategy. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample includes patient and control groups reported separately), I9 (reports within-task/unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (uses whole-brain contrasts with peak coordinates to define seeds), I11 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy; the experiment manipulated pain but did not ask participants to reappraise, accept, or otherwise intentionally regulate their emotions). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I6 (explicit instruction to regulate), which is required by the review’s inclusion criteria.

The study must be excluded because the regulated stimuli are script-driven imagery (participants imagined scenarios) rather than externally presented visual stimuli, so it fails inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli required). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: instructed suppression/'don't think'), I8 (acceptable sample), I9 (reports within-task regulation-related contrasts such as Don't Think > Think and Think Negative > Think Neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates), and I11 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria from E3–E7 apply. In summary: excluded because I7 not met (script-driven imagery/non-visual stimuli).

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli and reports unregulated viewing contrasts and whole-brain results; however the fMRI task did NOT instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, or other instructed regulation). The task involved passive viewing of faces and bodies with occasional attractiveness ratings, not instructed regulation. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 is not satisfied. Met inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrasts: Faces > Scrambled, Bodies > Scrambled), I10 (whole-brain group-level analyses with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (E3–E7: none met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Exclusion is based on missing I6 (instruction to regulate).

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample reported with patient and control groups), I9 (within-task contrasts: stress > neutral reported), I10 (whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses with MNI coordinates), I11 (results and coordinates clearly reported). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy — participants engaged in script-driven imagery without instructions to reappraise, accept, or otherwise regulate emotion), I7 (stimuli are script-driven auditory imagery, not visual stimuli such as pictures or films). Because the meta-analysis requires instructed emotion-regulation tasks of visual stimuli, failure to meet I6 and I7 warrants exclusion. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Met: I5 (task-based fMRI scan with an emotional task) and I8 (acceptable sample). Not met: I6 (no instruction to regulate emotion—participants were asked to rate how statements made them feel, not to reappraise or otherwise regulate), I7 (regulated/viewed stimuli are word/sentence statements presented as text—word/sentence stimuli are excluded), I9 (the paper does not report within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts such as "reappraise>look" or "emotion>baseline" for BOLD task data), and I10 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps/peak coordinates for the within-task contrasts are reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) from the review’s exclusion list apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Given these missing inclusion criteria, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal (reappraise vs attend). Emotional stimuli were visual (IAPS and validated alcohol images). The sample includes alcohol-dependent patients and matched healthy controls with results reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > attend per emotion; attend emotion > attend neutral) and whole-brain second-level voxelwise analyses with standard-space coordinates and corrected thresholds. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) with visual stimuli (video clips) during the task (I7), an acceptable sample (I8), and group-level whole-brain analyses with reported peak coordinates (I10,I11). The authors also report within-task regressions/contrasts related to task epochs (stressor vs baseline) and an emotion-induction regressor (I9). However, the study does NOT instruct participants to use any emotion-regulation strategy (no cognitive reappraisal, acceptance, distancing, or other instructed regulation); participants were told to ‘think back to the anagram task’ and to let thoughts come naturally while viewing videos. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) appear to apply, and the full text appears complete. Hence the study must be excluded because it fails to meet I6.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a labeling task (Label) versus viewing (View) with dynamic visual stimuli (videos of adolescent faces). The Label condition is an instructed task intended to engage implicit emotion regulation (affect labeling), and within-task contrasts (Label>View, Label>Blur, View>Blur) are reported. The study reports group-level whole-brain analyses (with thresholds, cluster-correction) and provides unthresholded maps and coordinates via NeuroVault. The sample (10–23 year-old females) meets the sample inclusion. No exclusion criteria apply: whole-brain task activation maps are reported, not ROI-only or connectivity-only, and there are within-task contrasts rather than only between-group effects. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and photos) and reports within-task contrasts for unregulated viewing (negative vs neutral) with whole-brain group analyses and peak coordinates. However, participants were not instructed to use any emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance); they simply viewed and rated pictures. Therefore the study does not meet the inclusion criterion requiring an instructed emotion-regulation task (I6). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered by the manuscript. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Exclusion criteria applied: []. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate emotion (explicit ‘decrease’ vs ‘look’ instructions), uses visual stimuli (IAPS pictures), reports within-task regulation and reactivity contrasts (decrease negative > look negative; look negative > look neutral), and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates/tables. Methods, results and discussion are fully reported. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study with instructed emotion regulation (conscious ‘imagine’ and spontaneous suppression priming), visual stimuli (colored squares as CS+ vs CS–), an appropriate sample, and within-task contrasts (threat>safe; suppression-primed vs unprimed), the reported results are based on region-of-interest (bilateral amygdala) percent signal change analyses. The paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space; analyses and inferences rely on ROI extraction only. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (ROI-only results) and fails inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise vs attend), using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures), with both an at-risk clinical group and healthy controls whose results are reported separately. The analyses include within-task contrasts for regulation (Reappraisal > Attend Negative) and unregulated viewing (View Negative > View Neutral), performed as group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak MNI coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports within-task effects, not purely perspective-taking). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise vs React) and reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > React) across three socio-emotional tasks. Two of the regulated stimulus types are visual (looming facial photographs and dynamic video clips of social criticism), which meet the review’s requirement for visual stimuli; although one task uses written autobiographical sentences, the presence of regulated visual stimuli suffices for inclusion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with thresholding and coordinates, and provides within-group and between-group task activation maps. Participant groups (SAD patients and healthy controls) are reported separately. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructed an emotion regulation strategy (detachment/distancing, a form of cognitive reappraisal) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS/EmoPicS images). It reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation and permit conditions (e.g., Negative Detach vs. Negative Permit) and conducts second-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space; ROI analyses are supplementary. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI results, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which children/adolescents were instructed to regulate emotional responses (cognitive reappraisal-style strategies: ‘pretend it’s fake’ or ‘pretend it’s right in front of you’) while viewing visual disgust-inducing images (IAPS and in-house images). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (decrease-gross > look-gross; increase-gross > look-gross) and unregulated viewing (look-gross > look-neutral). Group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (with cluster thresholds and Talairach coordinates). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (attend vs. reappraise) using visual stimuli (IAPS and alcohol images). Participant groups include AUD patients and healthy controls with group-specific analyses. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > attend; attend emotion > attend neutral) and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses reported at whole-brain FWE-corrected thresholds. The manuscript contains full introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This paper reports a task-based fMRI study in which participants were explicitly instructed to use cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative affect elicited by visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The methods describe block-wise Reappraise and Maintain conditions, online self-report ratings, and within-task contrasts including conjunctions ([Maintain > Baseline] AND [Reappraise > Baseline]) used to identify amygdala activation as well as task-dependent PPI contrasts (Reappraise > Maintain). Group-level, voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates (e.g., left amygdala MNI −22,0,−22) and whole-brain PPI results (Table 1, figures). The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation — reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (within-task contrasts related to regulation), I10 (group-level whole-brain maps with peak coordinates), and I11 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met (not only ROI/only connectivity-only; whole-brain task analyses are present). Full text appears complete.

This study meets several inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), explicitly instructs emotion regulation strategies including cognitive reappraisal and selective attention (I6), uses visual emotional stimuli in the form of film/video clips (I7), includes an eligible sample of younger and older adults (I8), and reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation and passive viewing (I9). However, all reported activation analyses were conducted within an explicit amygdala–PFC mask (region-limited search space), and the paper does not present a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation analysis with peak coordinates in standard space. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I10) and appears to report only region-of-interest / small-volume–restricted results, triggering exclusion criterion E4. Full text appears complete. Because I10 is not met and E4 applies, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that presents visual emotional stimuli (film clips) and reports within-task contrasts of emotion-evoking (EE) vs emotion-neutral (EN) conditions (EE−EN) using group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported significant clusters. The sample is acceptable (healthy adult groups). Although the task did not instruct an explicit emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal), the meta-analysis objective includes studies that involve unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., emotion > neutral), which this study provides. Full text includes introduction, methods (fMRI acquisition and analysis), results (behavioral, HRV, whole-brain contrasts) and discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for inclusion as an unregulated visual emotion-viewing fMRI study reporting whole-brain activation maps.

This study is excluded because the emotional stimuli regulated are not visual images or videos as required by I7. The task uses a competitive reaction-time paradigm with social provocation and auditory white-noise punishments; regulation instructions (reappraisal) target responses to provocation/auditory events rather than regulation of an emotional response to visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive reappraisal strategy), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task contrasts such as win>lose and lose>win), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), and I11 (whole-brain results described/tabled). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (emotional stimuli are not visual). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use emotion regulation strategies (reappraise, suppress, view) while viewing visual stimuli (IAPS and in-house pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > view, view > reappraise), behavioral and fMRI results, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-corrected thresholds and reported activation coordinates. The sample is healthy adults, and the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not a review, and task involves instructed regulation of emotional responses). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis (I5–I11). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal to regulate emotion elicited by visual stimuli (spider photographs). It reports within-task contrasts (regulate vs watch) and both ROI and whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses (with supplementary tables/figures), and follows participants (including clinical spider-phobic sample) with behavioral outcomes. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (and affect labeling) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Label > Observe, Reappraise > Observe, Label > Reappraise, etc.) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard space (SPM5, MNI coordinates). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: distancing reappraisal), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task reappraisal contrasts reported, e.g., R–NR), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported MNI peak coordinates), I11 (results reported in text/tables/figures). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I7 (emotional stimuli are VISUAL) — NOT MET: the regulated stimuli are anticipatory threat of shock (pain expectation) signaled auditorily; there are no visual emotional stimuli such as images or videos. Because the meta-analysis requires regulation of visual emotional stimuli, this study does not meet criterion I7 and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs emotion regulation (Reappraise > Maintain in the ERT) and includes unregulated viewing contrasts (Maintain > baseline, Fearful > Happy). Stimuli are visual (IAPS pictures and emotional faces). The paper reports within-task contrasts and describes voxel-wise, group-level whole-brain analysis with cluster correction and reports peak coordinates for DLPFC (x,y,z = −40,12,28), satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets the review inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) that instructs cognitive reappraisal as the regulation strategy (Regulate vs Attend; I6). The regulated stimuli are visual (colored CS squares and cigarette images; I7). The sample (adult smokers) is acceptable per criteria (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts directly assessing regulation (Attend CS+ vs Regulate CS+; I9). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects statistical maps were computed and thresholded (p<0.001) after normalization to standard (MNI) space, and activations (including right dACC, BA24/32) are reported in the text/figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements (I10, I11). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the emotional stimuli were script-driven mental imagery (written narrative scenarios) rather than visual stimuli (e.g., pictures, faces, film/video). Thus the study does not meet inclusion criterion I7 (visual emotional stimuli). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation via reappraisal/forgiveness instructions), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task regulation contrasts, e.g., forgiveness > unforgiveness), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses in standard space), I11 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria from the provided E3–E7 list apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded on the basis of failing I7 (script-driven imagery rather than visual stimuli).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of explicit emotion regulation using instructed strategies (reappraisal and response modulation) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., regulate > maintain, increase > decrease) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI peak coordinates for amygdala and PFC clusters. The sample (healthy young adults) is eligible and the full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not non-empirical, and not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise vs. Maintain) using visual IAPS images, in a clinical sample (anxiety and depression). The paper reports within-task contrast Reappraise>Maintain and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise regression analyses with peak MNI coordinates and cluster thresholds. Methods, results, and discussion are present, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task effects, and is not an empathy/perspective-taking-only design). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs participants to regulate emotional responses (explicit up-regulation via instructed imitation, IMT, and down-regulation via expressive suppression, eSUP) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (dynamic face video clips). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (IMT > eSUP, IMT > GND, eSUP > IMT, etc.) and conducts group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with coordinates and cluster reporting. The sample (20 healthy adults) is acceptable, and the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task effects, not an empathy task without regulation). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (mentalizing-reappraisal: up, down, look) during presentation of visual social stimuli (photos of proposers and monetary offers displayed on screen). The sample is healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., DOWN > LOOK, UP > LOOK, DOWN < LOOK < UP) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with cluster-corrected thresholds and peak coordinates (tables/figures). Reporting meets the meta-analysis requirements for whole-brain voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, and includes explicit instructions to amplify/dampen emotion). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I11 and should be included.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (fearful/angry faces) with a within-task unregulated viewing contrast (faces > shapes). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates and figures/tables, tests individual differences in reappraisal use but also provides the unregulated viewing contrast needed for the review. Although the study does not instruct emotion regulation (so it does not satisfy an instructed-regulation criterion), it meets the meta-analysis objective of including visual-stimulus viewing contrasts and provides whole-brain task activation maps appropriate for inclusion. Full text is complete.

This study does not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses; instead it manipulates financial incentive context (fixed wage vs performance-based) which may implicitly change emotion-related processing but does not meet the review’s requirement for an instructed regulation task. Exclusion criteria met: E7 (perspective-taking/self-or other-oriented task with no instruction to amplify or dampen emotion) applies because participants assumed a role and no regulation instruction was given. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—photos of faces), I8 (acceptable sample), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrasts such as emotion > neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates), I11 (results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no explicit instructed emotion regulation/cognitive reappraisal or similar). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which participants were instructed to regulate emotion (compassion meditation vs. cognitive reappraisal) while viewing visual images from the IAPS. The fMRI task includes Regulate and Attend conditions, and analyses report Negative–Neutral contrasts and Post–Pre training contrasts. The paper reports both ROI and whole-brain voxel-wise analyses, including a significant whole-brain cluster with MNI coordinates in right AI/OFC, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task activation maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study using an instructed cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task (regulate vs. look) with visual stimuli (IAPS photographs). It reports within-task contrasts for emotional reactivity (negative > neutral) and reappraisal (regulate negative > look negative) with group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and MNI peak coordinates (whole-brain FWE correction for regulate>look). Sample and analyses meet inclusion requirements. The full text is complete (background, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and not an empathy without regulation task).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (psychological distancing) during anticipation and stimulus periods, using visual IAPS social images. The sample includes avoidant patients and healthy controls reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation and unregulated viewing (e.g. Reappraise Cue>Look Cue, Reappraise Negative>Look Negative, Look Negative>Look Neutral) and provides group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates (text and supplemental tables/figures). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly compares instructed emotion-processing/acceptance ("permit") with passive viewing of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS). It meets inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instruction to permit/accept emotion—an antecedent-focused/acceptance strategy), I7 (visual stimuli—static IAPS pictures), I8 (healthy adult sample reported), I9 (within-task contrasts reported, e.g., permit > view, view negative > view neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise results and FWE-corrected clusters reported), and I11 (whole-brain results described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper is empirical with whole-brain task activation maps and within-group contrasts; it is not limited to ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, nor is it an empathy-perspective-taking-only task. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to perform cognitive reappraisal (downregulate/upregulate/maintain) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts of interest (downregulate > maintain, upregulate > maintain, negative > neutral) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses and ROI analyses, with statistical maps available on Neurovault. The sample includes younger and older adults and the analyses meet the meta-analysis requirements. Although some participants had incomplete brain coverage, whole-brain group-level results were nevertheless performed and reported. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) that instructs cognitive reappraisal as the regulation strategy (I6); stimuli are visual IAPS pictures presented during the task (I7); sample comprises healthy adult participants (I8); the paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g. RU–CU, CU–CN) (I9); a group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analysis is reported with peak coordinates and threshold (P<0.001) (I10); results are described in text and figures (I11). No exclusion criteria are met: this is empirical original fMRI activation work with whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This task-based fMRI study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. I5: It is a task-based fMRI experiment. I6: The protocol included an instructed regulation condition (“Reframe”), indicating an emotion-regulation strategy was part of the task battery. I7: Emotional stimuli were visual (looming faces, dynamic video clips, and visually-presented autobiographical sentences/negative self-beliefs); videos and written sentences are acceptable visual stimuli. I8: Participant sample is acceptable (clinical SAD group and healthy controls reported separately). I9: The paper reports within-task contrasts related to unregulated viewing (React versus Asterisks) for each task. I10: Whole-brain group-level analyses are reported with cluster coordinates and tables. I11: Whole-brain results are clearly described in text/tables. No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only ROI results, only connectivity, or only between-group effects without within-task effects. Full text appears complete (includes background, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion.

This is a task-based (event-related) fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (faces) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (angry>neutral, fearful>neutral, happy>neutral) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and peak coordinates (FDR-corrected). Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given (I6 not met), the meta-analysis objective explicitly accepts studies where participants view emotional stimuli without regulating; the study therefore satisfies the unregulated-viewing criterion (I9). The full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (whole-brain group-level analysis with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Given these points, the study is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis examining neural responses during viewing (unregulated) of visual emotional stimuli.

This is an empathy/perspective-taking fMRI study (video-based empathic accuracy task) without any instruction to regulate participants’ own emotions (no reappraisal/distancing/acceptance etc.). It therefore meets exclusion criterion E7 (empathy/perspective-taking without instructed emotion regulation). It does meet multiple inclusion items (I5: task-based fMRI; I7: visual stimuli—videos; I8: eligible sample—adolescents; I9: reports within-task contrasts/unregulated viewing contrasts (empathic-accuracy trials vs baseline); I10: whole-brain voxel-wise analyses reported; I11: results clearly described). However it fails I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), and E7 applies. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study (Go/NoGo) using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) and reports an unregulated viewing contrast (aversive > neutral) as a whole-brain, voxelwise group analysis with reported peak coordinates. The task is not an instructed emotion-regulation paradigm (no reappraisal instruction), but the meta-analysis objective accepts unregulated viewing contrasts. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for unregulated visual emotional stimulus viewing analyses (I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11) and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and suppression) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (video clips). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise/suppress > watch), presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (Talairach), and includes full methods, results, and discussion. The sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study reports only ROI-based task analyses and does not provide any group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or peak coordinates (Exclusion E4). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy was used — recall of positive autobiographical memories), I7 (visual emotional stimuli were used in the view condition — IAPS pictures), I8 (sample qualifies — healthy human participants), I9 (within-task contrasts reported, e.g. regulate > baseline, view > baseline, regulate > view). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain group-level task activation maps / peak coordinates reported; task results are reported as ROI analyses). Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet two required inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis: I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy) and I7 (emotional stimuli are visual images/film). Instead, the fMRI tasks directed participants to engage in rumination (provocation-focused, self-focused, neutral-focused), which is not an instructed regulation strategy such as reappraisal/acceptance, and the emotional stimuli/feedback and prompts were presented as written text (word/sentence stimuli). The study does meet several other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (eligible sample with group results), I9 (reports within-task contrasts such as feedback > pre-feedback baseline and provocation-focus > neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates), and I11 (coordinates/whole-brain results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded for failure to satisfy I6 and I7.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual negative pictures (I7) in a healthy sample (I8) and it reports within-task contrasts comparing inhibition-priming versus neutral-priming (I9). However, the study did not instruct participants to use any explicit emotion-regulation strategy; it used word-priming to induce automatic (implicit) regulation rather than an instructed regulation task, so it does not meet I6. Moreover, the reported neuroimaging results are presented via an ROI-focused analysis (exploratory ROI percent-signal-change and ROI-based contrasts) with no accompanying whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation tables or peak coordinates described, which fails I10 and corresponds to exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI/ small-volume results with no whole-brain analysis). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) with an eligible sample (I8) that reports within-task contrasts (Tenderness vs Anguish) and provides group-level whole-brain, FWE-corrected results with peak coordinates (I9, I10). However, it does NOT meet key inclusion requirements: I6 (the task does not instruct a canonical emotion-regulation strategy applied to an external stimulus such as cognitive reappraisal/acceptance/reality-checking; participants were instructed to generate/up-regulate internal emotional states via personalized recall/mantras and neurofeedback) and I7 (the regulated/emotion-eliciting stimuli were primarily non-visual: music and autobiographical imagery; the virtual environment served as neurofeedback/BCI rather than as the visual emotional stimulus to be regulated). No exclusion criteria from the review (E3–E7) are directly triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to satisfy I6 and I7 required by the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS photographs) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (Negative > Neutral and arousal-specific contrasts) analyzed at the group level with whole-brain random-effects maps and reported peak coordinates. The sample (young and older adults) is acceptable. Although the reported results focus on a spontaneous viewing/run before any instructed emotion-regulation manipulation (so no instructed reappraisal contrast is analyzed here), the meta-analysis objective explicitly includes studies that view stimuli without regulating; therefore the study meets the relevant inclusion path. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (acceptable sample), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses), I11 (coordinates/results clearly described). No exclusion criteria were met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation using visual stimuli (aversive pictures). The methods explicitly instruct participants to down-regulate emotional responses, report within-task contrasts (REGULATE vs VIEW, REGULATE>NEUTRAL, VIEW>NEUTRAL), and present group-level whole-brain analyses with peaks (e.g., right amygdala peak coordinates) and cluster-corrected results. Sample is healthy females (eligible). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria I5-I11 are met, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.
