Full text appears complete.

Exclusion E5 applies: the study reports only seed-based task connectivity (amygdala seed) results rather than whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Although it contains a task contrast (Violence > Non-Violence) and reports voxelwise connectivity maps with peak coordinates, these are connectivity (seed-to-voxel) analyses and no conventional whole-brain task activation (e.g., emotion > neutral) activation map is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: violent video game clips), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrast analogue, PLAC Violence > PLAC Non-Violence), I10 (group-level voxelwise maps with MNI coordinates provided for connectivity results), I11 (results described in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: [] (none additionally unmet beyond the connectivity-only issue). Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment using visual emotional stimuli (faces) and reports within-task contrasts for unregulated viewing (e.g., emotion > shape) with whole-brain group analyses and reported coordinates. However, it does not instruct participants to apply an explicit emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, acceptance, distancing) — tasks are matching and Stroop paradigms requiring cognitive control but not an instructed emotion-regulation strategy. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion E4 applies: the study reports primarily ROI/mask-based voxelwise analyses (a priori ROIs: left/right amygdala and insula; exploratory larger ROI mask) and does not present a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map in standard space. Consequently inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. The study does satisfy: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed implicit emotion-regulation paradigm via attend/ignore instructions qualifies as instructed cognitive control), I7 (visual stimuli—faces and houses), I8 (sample reported; clinical group with controls), and I9 (within-task contrasts related to regulation/attention: attend vs ignore fearful faces and emotion×attention interactions). Because I10 is not met and E4 is triggered (ONLY ROI/mask results), the study is excluded from the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (IAPS) with healthy adult participants; it reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts for valence and arousal and presents group-level whole-brain statistical maps. However, the task involved incidental emotion rating and did not instruct any emotion regulation strategy nor report any emotion-regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look), so it does not meet inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to satisfy I6 (instruction to regulate).

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional face stimuli and an instructed effortful regulation paradigm (n-back with emotional distractors), reporting within-task contrasts and MNI coordinates; however all neuroimaging analyses were conducted within an a priori region-of-interest mask (frontolimbic and striatal ROIs) and no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps or analyses are reported. Per the review criteria, studies that report ONLY ROI or small-volume-corrected results with no whole-brain analysis must be excluded (E4). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive control/effortful emotion regulation via task demands), I7 (visual stimuli—faces), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task contrasts reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation map reported). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (ER and CR tasks) that explicitly instructed an emotion regulation strategy (reappraise/savoring) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS and smoking images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise vs view; smoking cue vs neutral) entered into group-level repeated-measures random-effects analyses and describes significant group×time whole-brain effects (cluster-corrected) in rACC and ventral striatum, and reports seed-to-voxel rsFC analyses. Core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present, and whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (clusters within standard anatomical space), satisfying the review’s criteria. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

Exclusion due to E4 and E5: the study reports only ROI-based connectivity/graph analyses (Dependency Network Analysis) on a predefined set of regions and does not present any group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps or peak coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI: participants viewed a film in the scanner), I7 (visual stimuli: film/video clip), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task contrast: high vs. low anger epochs were compared). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy—participants passively viewed the clip; regulation was implicit/not instructed), I10 (no whole-brain group-level task-evoked voxelwise maps or reported peak coordinates). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded because it violates E4 and E5 while lacking required whole-brain activation evidence (I10) and does not implement instructed regulation (I6).

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (faces) and reports task contrasts (e.g., informative vs. confirmatory feedback; high vs. low emotional intensity) with peak coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample ok), I9 (within-task emotion-related contrasts such as high vs. low intensity), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I11 (coordinates and results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 — participants were NOT instructed to use an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other instructed regulation); the study examined implicit/automatic regulation but did not include an instructed regulation condition or contrast (e.g., reappraise > look). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional face stimuli and reports unregulated emotion contrasts, but it does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain task-evoked activation reporting. Specifically, the paper focuses on ROI-based activation and dynamic causal modeling (effective connectivity) among vmPFC, sgACC, and amygdala, and does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates. Therefore it falls under exclusions for ROI-only/effective-connectivity-only reporting.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to label affect (an instructed strategy shown to function as incidental emotion regulation), using visual stimuli (photographs of faces). The sample includes GAD patients and healthy controls with group-level analyses. The paper reports within-task contrasts (emotion vs. fixation; affect vs. gender) and longitudinal regulation-related contrasts (pre–post changes, group-by-time interactions) and provides whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task effects, not an empathy/perspective-taking-only paradigm). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual stimuli (video clips; I7) with an eligible sample (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts (separation vs play; unregulated viewing contrast) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with reported peak clusters (I9, I10, I11). However, the fMRI task did not instruct participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing instructions); participants simply viewed own and unfamiliar child play and separation scenes. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation) is not met, and per the requirement that all inclusion criteria be satisfied this study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses rather than a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Exclusion criteria met: E4. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed emotion-control strategy: participants were instructed to ignore emotional distractors/engage voluntary attentional control), I7 (visual stimuli: emotional faces), I8 (sample includes patients and matched healthy controls reported separately), I9 (reports within-task contrasts related to emotion presence/regulation: emotional-face vs no-face contrasts during 2-back). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps with peak coordinates reported; analyses were ROI-based). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded for failing I10 and meeting exclusion E4.

This study is excluded because it reports resting-state functional connectivity analyses only and does not include any task-based emotion regulation fMRI or task-evoked whole-brain activation contrasts. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I8 (sample: any participant group). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli used in a regulation task), I9 (no within-task emotion regulation or viewing contrasts), I10 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual fearful-face stimuli and an eligible sample (I5, I7, I8 satisfied). However, it does not meet key inclusion requirements: the task does not implement a clearly instructed emotion-regulation strategy of the type specified (e.g., reappraisal/acceptance/cognitive control)—participants performed self-labeling (rating subjective fear), which is closer to affect-labeling and was not framed/reported as an instruction to regulate (I6 not met). Critically, the paper reports ROI-based effective connectivity (dynamic effective connectivity/Granger causality) and ROI eigenvariate activation analyses without presenting any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or peak coordinates. Thus it violates exclusion criteria E4 and E5 (only ROI/effective-connectivity results reported, no whole-brain activation maps). It also fails to report the within-task whole-brain contrasts related to regulation or unregulated viewing required by I9/I10. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is a study protocol (RCT) describing planned task-based fMRI with visual IAPS stimuli in BPD patients, but it contains no original fMRI results, no reported within-task contrasts, and no whole-brain peak coordinates. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (non-empirical/protocol without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI planned), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS pictures), I8 (sample described, clinical and healthy groups). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation task; participants are instructed to watch and rate pictures, not to regulate emotion), I9 (does not report any within-task contrast results such as reappraise>look or emotion>baseline), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task activation maps or coordinates reported). Therefore this article should be excluded from the meta-analysis based on E3 and failure to meet I6, I9, and I10.

This study meets several inclusion criteria (I5: task-based fMRI; I6: an instructed emotion-regulation/self-focused strategy—emotion-introspection—was used; I8: clinical sample reported; I9: within-task contrasts related to the instructed strategy were reported (e.g. ‘feel’>‘think’, ‘feel’>‘neutral’); I10/I11: group-level whole-brain analyses and coordinates/thresholding are reported). However it fails the stimulus requirement (I7): the regulated emotional content was internally generated (participants introspected on their current emotions) rather than regulation of visually presented emotional stimuli. The only visual material were neutral IAPS distractor images presented after trials, not emotional visual stimuli to be regulated. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore I exclude the study because it does not satisfy I7 (visual emotional stimuli).

This report is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to apply a mindfulness emotion-regulation strategy during the anticipation and perception of negative/ambiguous visual stimuli (IAPS). It uses visual stimuli, includes within-task contrasts (e.g. expectation negative vs neutral; perception negative vs neutral) and reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates (e.g. DMPFC x = -7, y = 7, z = -54). The sample (healthy adult participants) and analyses meet the review’s sample and analytic requirements. ROI results are presented but are accompanied by whole-brain results and tables/figures, so the study is not limited to ROI-only reporting. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI perspective-taking study using visual IAPS images and reports whole-brain group analyses, but participants were instructed to predict others’ affect (adopt others’ perspective) rather than instructed to use an emotion regulation strategy to amplify or dampen their own emotional response. Exclusion E7 applies (perspective-taking with no regulation instruction). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task contrasts/unregulated viewing reported), I10 (whole-brain group analyses reported), I11 (results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal/distancing/explicit regulation). Therefore the study must be excluded per E7.

This article meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal strategies (decrease/increase) (I6), employs visual stimuli (IAPS images) (I7), includes an adolescent sample (I8), reports within-task contrasts for both regulation and passive viewing (e.g., decrease > look negative; look negative > neutral) (I9), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction (standard-space results described and reported; supplemental/tables referenced) meeting whole-brain evidence requirements (I10,I11). Core methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies on regulation/viewing of visual emotional stimuli.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructed emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and distraction) using visual negative images (IAPS), meeting I5–I7. Participants include younger and older adults (I8). Analyses report within-task contrasts and univariate GLM comparisons of regulation conditions (reappraise vs distract and distract/reappraise > baseline) and behavioral outcomes (I9). The paper describes whole-brain voxelwise univariate analyses with cluster-thresholded statistics and reports peak maxima in tables (Table 2), satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting (I10, I11). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, not empathy-without-regulation). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (reality check / cognitive reappraisal) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures; also video transfer task). The sample (healthy adults) is eligible. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., regulate > view, regulate > baseline) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses (voxel-wise thresholds, cluster corrections) with reported clusters/coordinates. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to engage in self-referential emotion regulation (imagining experiencing positive-social scenes), i.e., an instructed regulation strategy (up-regulation via perspective-taking). Stimuli are visual (IAPS/NAPS/GAPED images). The sample is a healthy volunteer group with group-level results reported. The paper reports within-task contrasts (regulation > viewing; positive > neutral; task × stimulus interaction) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (FWE-corrected), satisfying reporting requirements. Full text contains Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in adolescent girls that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (‘‘decrease’’/distancing) during an emotion regulation paradigm using visual stimuli (IAPS and youth images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., decrease > look; look negative > look neutral) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak activations and cluster correction in standard space. The full text includes introduction, methods (tasks, acquisition, preprocessing, ROI/PPI), results (behavioral, whole-brain, ROI, connectivity), and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal (decrease vs look contrasts) with visual stimuli (IAPS images). The sample includes adolescents (clinical subgroup with suicidal ideation and controls). The paper reports within-task contrasts (decrease > look; look negative > look neutral) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with reported cluster peaks. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment. All inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text reports an empirical task-based fMRI study in which participants were instructed to regulate emotion using a distancing (cognitive reappraisal) strategy while viewing visually presented negative and neutral images (I5, I6, I7). The sample includes a clinical group (PMDD) and healthy controls with results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation-related contrasts (negative, far > negative, close) and unregulated viewing contrasts (negative > neutral) (I9). It also presents whole-brain, voxel-wise group analyses with peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space and cluster-corrected results (I10,I11). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review and is included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use attentional deployment (directing gaze toward or away from arousing regions) as an emotion regulation strategy while viewing visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (unpleasant non-arousing focus vs. natural viewing; unpleasant arousing focus vs. natural viewing), group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with coordinates and tables, and concurrent eye-tracking and connectivity analyses. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; includes whole-brain activation maps; not connectivity-only; within-group effects reported; not an empathy-only perspective-taking task).

This study is excluded because it does not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses (inclusion criterion I6 not met). It is a task-based fMRI study (I5), uses visual stimuli (faces) (I7), includes an eligible sample (I8), reports within-task emotional contrasts/unregulated viewing effects (I9), and describes group-level whole-brain analyses in standard (Talairach) space with supplementary results (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Specifically: Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy or regulation contrast such as reappraise>look). Full text judged complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based, empirical fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation via cognitive reappraisal ("decrease" cue) and uses visual stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (NEU, NEG, NER; NEU vs NEG, NEU vs NER, NEG vs NER) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps with cluster-based correction, from a healthy adult sample. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli, whole-brain group-level analyses, and within-task contrasts reported. However, participants were not instructed to use any emotion-regulation strategy; they passively viewed facial primes and pictures and rated arousal. Inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy) is not met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes instructed emotion regulation (volitional cognitive reappraisal) and unregulated picture viewing contrasts. Task 5 explicitly has subjects reappraising negative/positive/neutral pictures (visual stimuli) with R > NR contrasts; Task 4 uses instructed distancing reappraisal of visually presented threat/safety cues. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM), and within-task contrasts relevant to regulation and viewing are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task effects, not an empathy-only perspective-taking task). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which participants were instructed to process/implement emotion-regulation reappraisals (guided creative and ordinary cognitive reappraisal) while viewing negative visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The sample (healthy college adults) is eligible. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., creative > ordinary, creative > objective) and trial-by-trial covariates, with group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and reported thresholds/coordinates (SPM8, cluster-level FWE, voxel-level coordinates). Reporting of whole-brain results and coordinate tables/contrasts satisfies the meta-analysis reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion rationale: The study is excluded because it does not meet all required inclusion criteria. Exclusion IDs met: E4 (reports ROI-based/connectivity results without a whole-brain voxelwise task activation analysis) and E5 (reports primarily effective/connectivity analyses without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli — sad/neutral faces), I8 (sample includes patients and controls), I9 (reports an unregulated viewing contrast, negative > neutral). Inclusion IDs NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation task or reappraisal; participants performed a gender-identification flanker task without instructions to regulate emotion), I10 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported; analyses were ROI- and connectivity-focused). Therefore the paper is ineligible for the meta-analysis as defined.

This full text meets all required inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study using instructed cognitive reappraisal (I5,I6); stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7); participants are healthy adults with reported sample characteristics (I8); analyses include within-task contrasts comparing reappraise vs look (ReappNeg > LookNeg) (I9); group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates and FDR correction are provided (I10); whole-brain results are reported in text/tables/figures (I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is empirical original fMRI work, reports whole-brain activation maps/coordinates, and includes within-group task effects. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion); supplemental material availability is noted but not required. Hence INCLUDE.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs cognitive reappraisal of visual (face) stimuli and reports within-task contrasts (reappraise vs look), and thus meets several inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the neuroimaging results are reported using an a priori amygdala ROI/masking approach and parameter estimates from that ROI; no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map with peak coordinates in standard space is provided in the supplied full text. Therefore it appears the paper reports only ROI-masked (SVC) results without a qualifying whole-brain task activation map, which violates exclusion criterion E4. Because I10 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise map with coordinates) is not met, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Full text presents a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) with visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise>Maintain) at the group level and gives peak coordinates in MNI space. Both a clinical PTSD group and a combat-exposed control group are included and analyzed. Although primary inference used an ROI mask with cluster correction, the authors also conducted whole-brain analyses (reported as yielding no additional significant clusters), and group-level voxelwise maps with standard-space peaks are provided. The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS) and reports within-task contrasts comparing negative versus neutral trials (attending and ignoring conditions). It provides group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with MNI coordinates and tables/figures, and the full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction (reappraisal) was used, the review objective allows unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., emotion > neutral), which this paper reports. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, empathy/perspective-taking-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal during an emotion regulation task using visual stimuli (IAPS images). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > Look; Reappraise > implicit baseline) and group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates (e.g., left IFG), fulfilling whole-brain reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) with instructed cognitive regulation (reappraisal/suppression; I6), reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., regulation vs nonregulation; I9), provides group-level whole-brain analyses and coordinates (I10,I11), and the sample is acceptable (I8). However, the regulated stimuli are not visual emotional images/videos: the task uses mental arithmetic with time pressure and social feedback (a psychosocial stress task), so the emotional elicitors are non-visual task/stressors rather than visual emotional stimuli, failing inclusion criterion I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore EXCLUDED because it does not meet I7 (visual stimuli requirement).

The paper reports an empirical, task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults where participants were explicitly instructed to use cognitive reappraisal (CR) and attention deployment (AD) during presentation of visual IAPS images. The study provides within-task contrasts (CR>AD, AD>CR) from first- and group-level GLM analyses, and reports group-level whole-brain statistical maps (data were transformed to Talairach space, FDR/FWE-corrected results described and shown in figures/tables). Amygdala ROI and seed-based connectivity analyses are supplementary but whole-brain task activation is reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Limitations, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli — IAPS images), I8 (adolescent sample), I9 (within-task contrasts: Decrease>Look, Increase>Look). However the paper does not report a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation map with peak coordinates in a standard space (I10 not met). The analyses are primarily ROI/parcellation-based (DLPFC parcels) with an exploratory parcel-based whole-brain parcel analysis, and no voxelwise coordinate tables or standard-space peak coordinates are presented. This means the study reports only region-of-interest/parcellation results without an accompanying voxelwise whole-brain map, so it violates exclusion criterion E4. Therefore exclude.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the SEAT paradigm with instructed implicit emotion regulation (Like/Dislike appraisal and attention-shift conditions). Stimuli are visual (static images of faces and scenes). The sample is healthy adults. The paper reports within-task emotion-regulation contrasts (Like/Dislike − Male/Female; Indoor/Outdoor − Male/Female) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and FWE correction. Reporting includes tables and text describing results. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis: although it is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study (I5) with an eligible sample (I8) and reports group-level whole-brain results (I10) and acceptable reporting (I11), it does NOT instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met). The paradigm used math and word verification tasks that incidentally evoke anxiety rather than instructions to reappraise or otherwise regulate emotional responses; stimuli are cognitive problems rather than visual emotional stimuli of the type required (I7 not met). The paper also does not report within-task contrasts specifically labeling instructed emotion regulation (I9 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation in late-life GAD and meets several inclusion items (I5: task-based fMRI; I6: instructed reappraisal/worry reappraisal; I8: acceptable sample; I9: within-task contrasts via condition-specific connectivity maps; I11: results reported with peak coordinates). However it fails I7 because the regulated stimuli are personalized worry scripts/sentences presented on screen (script-driven imagery/word/sentence stimuli), not the visual image/video stimuli required. Critically, the study reports only seed-based functional connectivity (seed-to-voxel) analyses and does not report whole-brain task-evoked activation maps; this triggers exclusion criterion E5 (ONLY seed-based connectivity without whole-brain task activation maps). Therefore the paper must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to regulate emotion (diminish/enhance/maintain) using cognitive reappraisal-like strategies during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (diminish>maintain, enhance>maintain, maintain>diminish) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and thresholding. The sample includes clinical (PTSD, trauma-exposed non-PTSD) and healthy control groups with separate reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use distancing (a form of cognitive reappraisal) to inhibit emotion (meets I5 and I6). Stimuli were visual IAPS pictures (I7). Sample is healthy adults (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (feel vs inhibit; endogenous vs exogenous inhibition) (I9). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates in MNI space and tables/figures (I10,I11). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and references (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, not empathy-only). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to regulate emotional responses using interpersonal cognitive reappraisal (disengage, view, engage) while viewing visual stimuli (IAPS and photographs). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts (disengage>view, engage>view, linear contrasts) and unregulated viewing contrasts (negative>neutral), presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates, and includes full Methods, Results, and Discussion. Sample (24 healthy women) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, and includes instructed regulation). Full text appears complete. Based on these points the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of responses to maternal versus stranger visual stimuli and reports amygdala reactivity and seed-based PPI connectivity. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli - face images), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task/unregulated viewing contrasts such as mother vs stranger). However, the study does NOT meet I6: there was no instructed emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal or other instructed regulation) during the fMRI task. It also does NOT meet I10: the paper does not report a group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates in standard space; the reported imaging results focus on ROI (amygdala) analyses and seed-based PPI connectivity. Thus exclusion criterion E5 applies (reports only seed-based connectivity/ROI without a whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal) using visual IAPS images in adults with anxiety disorders, and reports condition-specific activations used in prediction models. However, the analyses are based on average activations in 70 anatomically defined ROIs and the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates in standard space. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports ONLY ROI-based results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis) and does not meet inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain voxelwise group map).

Although this study uses task-based fMRI (NF and backward-masking/emotional conflict tasks) and reports whole-brain group-level results with peak coordinates, it does not meet the review's core requirement that participants be instructed to regulate an emotional response to visual stimuli (I6). The fMRI tasks primarily involve neurofeedback-driven downregulation of amygdala activity (NF vs rest), i.e., volitional modulation of a neural signal, rather than an instructed emotion regulation strategy applied to concurrently presented visual emotional stimuli (e.g., reappraisal of pictures). While visual stimulus tasks (backward masking; emotional conflict Stroop) are present, regulation was not instructed during those stimulus presentations. Therefore I6 is not satisfied; additionally, the within-task contrasts involving regulation do not specifically reflect instructed emotion regulation of visual stimuli as required (I9 is not met for the meta-analysis target). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I9. Exclusion criteria met: none.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study with appropriate within-task contrasts (SC>NT, SP>NT) and whole-brain, group-level analyses reported (satisfying I5, I9, I10, and I11), it does not meet critical inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. The experiment did not instruct participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal, acceptance, distancing, or other regulated instructions)—participants were asked to focus on the meaning and any emotional responses, not to regulate them (I6 not met). Crucially, the emotional stimuli are words/adjectives presented visually; the review’s stimulus inclusion specifically excludes word/sentence stimulus studies (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal and distraction) using visual IAPS stimuli and includes patient and control groups. It reports within-task contrasts (distraction vs reappraisal) and extensive PPI-based connectivity/network analyses. However, the manuscript presents ROI-based gPPI connectivity analyses and network contingency results across parcellated ROIs rather than reporting any group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps with peak coordinates in standard space. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I10 (and I11) requiring whole-brain task activation evidence and meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only PPI/effective connectivity without whole-brain activation results). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I10, I11. Exclusion criteria met: E5.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation with visual stimuli (I5, I7), includes an appropriate sample (I8), and reports an unregulated within-task contrast (negative > positive) relevant to emotion processing (I9). However, it does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy during the fMRI task (I6 not met), and the provided full text does not report peak coordinates from a group-level whole-brain statistical map in standard stereotactic space (I10 not met). Although whole-brain analyses are described and supplementary images are referenced, peak coordinates are not present in the supplied content; therefore not all inclusion criteria are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered based on the provided text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS and spider photographs). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (e.g. up > look, down > look) and unregulated viewing contrasts (spider > aversive, spider > neutral). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates in MNI space (tables and text), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study with instructed emotion regulation (subjects cued to reduce positive or negative emotion), using visual stimuli (IAPS and images), and reporting within-subject contrasts (regulate vs view). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed with peak coordinates in MNI space and conjunction/contrast results described. Full methods, results, and discussion are present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli and whole-brain group analyses (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11). However, participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses (no reappraisal/other instructed regulation); the task was an oddball target detection with aversive distractors, so inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I6).

This study is EXCLUDED because it does not meet all required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrast: CS+E vs CS–), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak MNI coordinates), I11 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy during the fMRI task — participants performed fear conditioning/extinction and recall but were not instructed to regulate emotion in-scanner), I7 (stimulus modality not explicitly stated as VISUAL in the full text provided — the conditioned stimuli modality is not clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Because I7 (visual stimuli) is not confirmed and I6 (instructed regulation) is absent, the study does not satisfy all inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study with instructed emotion regulation (down-regulation via real-time fMRI neurofeedback) using visual aversive pictures in healthy participants, and it reports within-task contrasts (‘regulate > view’) in connectivity analyses. However, the paper presents only seed-based connectivity (PPI) and effective connectivity (DCM) results and does not report a group-level, whole-brain task activation map (task-evoked activation contrasts with whole-brain coordinates) within this full text (activation results are referenced as reported in a prior paper). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ONLY seed-based/effective connectivity reported without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked activation map reported in this article). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli and whole-brain group analyses, it does not meet the key requirement that an emotion-regulation strategy was instructed. The task induced regret via feedback about missed opportunities, but participants were not instructed to reappraise, distance, accept, or otherwise regulate their emotional responses; the study measured natural/regulatory differences between groups rather than an instructed regulation manipulation. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (within-task contrasts for emotional vs non-emotional outcomes), I10 (whole-brain group analyses), I11 (reporting of whole-brain results). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (Reappraise vs Look Negative) using visual IAPS images in a sample of social anxiety disorder patients. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraise > Look Negative), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and cluster correction in standard (MNI) space. The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. These features satisfy the review inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructed a cognitive emotion regulation strategy (imagery-based reappraisal) during presentation of visual stimuli (colored squares). The paper reports within-task contrasts directly addressing regulation (Attend vs Regulate CS+), uses group-level whole-brain GLM analyses with reported coordinates, and contains full methods, results, and discussion. Participants are healthy adults and analyses include SCR-behavior correlations. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I11. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion E4 applies: the paper reports ROI analyses of the right amygdala (parent vs stranger contrast) and no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps or peak coordinates are presented in the main text (no evidence of whole-brain coordinate tables/figures). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: parent/stranger photographs), I8 (sample: children/adolescents), I9 (within-task contrast: parent > stranger/unregulated viewing contrasts). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation; participants simply viewed parent/stranger images), I10 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps/coordinates reported). Because E4 is met (only ROI results reported), the study must be excluded for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (fear and neutral faces; I7) in an eligible sample (adults; I8). The paper reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (fear > neutral anticipation) and within-group effects (I9). The authors also performed and reported an exploratory whole-brain voxel-wise analysis with cluster thresholds and coordinates (I10, I11). Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given (I6 not applicable for unregulated-viewing studies), the meta-analysis objective permits inclusion of unregulated viewing studies. Full text is complete and contains methods, results, and coordinates for whole-brain analyses. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for inclusion as an unregulated viewing task-based fMRI study of visual emotional stimuli.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes an instructed emotion-regulation condition (distraction) as well as appraisal and passive viewing conditions. Visual stimuli (individually tailored pictures) were used. The sample includes unmedicated OCD patients and matched healthy controls with group-level results reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g. appraisal > baseline; OCD-relevant > aversive) and PPI analyses, and displays whole-brain task-evoked activation (GLM task effect; Supplementary Table S2) with peak coordinates in standard space. Reporting in main text, figures, and supplementary material satisfies whole-brain evidence requirements. None of the exclusion criteria apply: the paper is empirical (not a review), includes whole-brain activation maps in addition to connectivity analyses (so not only ROI/seed-based results), reports within-group task effects, and is not an empathy/perspective-taking study. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study with bereaved and control groups and reports whole-brain Grief > Neutral contrasts with MNI peak coordinates, it does not meet critical inclusion criteria for this review. The ecStroop task used idiographic word stimuli (grief-related words), and the review excludes studies whose stimuli are word/sentence-based rather than visual images or video (I7 not met). Additionally, participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing instruction), so I6 (instructed regulation) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Decision: EXCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study (N=24) that instructed participants to regulate emotion using cognitive reappraisal (decrease) versus view, with visual IAPS pictures as stimuli. The paper reports within-task contrasts (decrease–view) and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with FWE cluster-corrected results, figures and tables of coordinates, as well as ROI analyses. Participant sample details and full methods, results and discussion are provided in the full text. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal/distancing to suppress sadness (methods: explicit reappraisal training and instructions). Emotional stimuli are visual film clips (qualifies per I7). Sample: healthy children (girls aged 8–10) — eligible per I8. Analyses include within-task contrasts and an interaction contrast isolating regulation effects (e.g., Sadness/Reappraisal vs Sadness/No Reappraisal), and report group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (SPM99), with tables of loci—meeting I9–I11. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (no-only-ROI, connectivity-only, or non-empirical issues). Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria.

While this is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (I5, I7) with an eligible sample (BD patients and healthy controls; I8), reporting valence contrasts (Negative > Neutral) and providing group-level coordinates/figures (I9, I10, I11), it does NOT instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses. The paradigm presents affective images as irrelevant background distractors during a cognitive interference task (MSIT), but there is no instructed emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraise, down-regulate, accept) or regulation cue period. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation) is not met, and the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it reports only resting-state fMRI analyses and does not provide any within-task emotion-regulation contrasts or whole-brain task activation maps. Exclusion ID met: E5 (reported only resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (a task-based fMRI session with an emotion regulation task was performed), I6 (an instructed emotion regulation strategy was used), I7 (visual stimuli — fearful pictures), I8 (sample qualifies: OCD patients and healthy controls). Inclusion IDs NOT met: I9 (no within-task contrast related to emotion regulation or unregulated viewing is reported in the paper), I10 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or peak coordinates are provided). Because the paper’s analyses and reported results are limited to resting-state network predictors of rTMS response, it does not fulfill the meta-analysis requirement for reported task-evoked whole-brain activation contrasts. Full text appears complete.

This study should be excluded because it is not a task-based emotion regulation fMRI study. It uses resting-state fMRI effective connectivity (DCM) and diffusion MRI (DTI) tractography, with no instructed emotion-regulation task, no within-task regulation contrasts, and no whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only resting-state/effective connectivity and structural analyses without any whole-brain task activation). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample includes clinical and control groups). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation task), I9 (reports within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), I10 (whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded from the meta-analysis focusing on task-based emotion regulation fMRI.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal: enhance/suppress/maintain) using visual IAPS pictures, with a sample of healthy participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., suppress > maintain, enhance > maintain) and uses whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (data normalized to Talairach space; cluster-size thresholding reported) including voxelwise PPI connectivity maps. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

The study is EXCLUDED because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: the fMRI task did not instruct an explicit emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, acceptance, instructed cognitive control). Instead it probes automatic regulation of emotional conflict (iI–cI) without instruction. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—faces), I8 (sample includes eligible ages), I9 (reports within-task contrasts indexing emotion conflict and conflict regulation), I10 (reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates), and I11 (coordinates/results described and in supplementary material). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because the review requires instructed/regulation tasks (I6), this automatic/uninstructed regulation paradigm does not qualify for inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a visual faces task (faces > shapes) that evokes affective processing. It reports within-task contrasts (faces > shapes) at the group level, with second-level voxelwise analyses in SPM5 and figures/tables (MNI reference) indicating whole-brain task-evoked results. The sample includes clinical (late-life depressed) and control groups reported separately. Analyses are not restricted to ROI-only or connectivity-only approaches. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for visual-task or unregulated viewing fMRI studies and provides whole-brain coordinates/activation maps suitable for inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs emotion regulation (DECREASE trials using reappraisal/distancing strategies) during presentation of visual stimuli (static IAPS photographs). It reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g. Decrease > Watch, Watch > Decrease) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates in standard space (MNI, converted to Talairach). Sample and methods are described and the full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only reporting, no connectivity-only analyses, not a non-empirical paper, and the task includes instructed regulation rather than mere perspective-taking). Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria (I5–I11).

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli and it reports within-task emotional vs neutral contrasts, the manuscript’s primary reported neuroimaging results are seed-based PPI (effective/connectivity) analyses conducted within anatomical ROIs (amygdala seed and MPFC/ACC mask). The paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates to qualify under the whole-brain activation requirement. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E5 (reports only seed-based/effective connectivity without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (results are ROI-masked/ROI-based with no whole-brain analysis). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli - faces), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrast emotional vs neutral). Inclusion criteria not met: I10 (no whole-brain group-level task activation map reported), and I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy). Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed an emotion regulation strategy (attentional deployment) during anticipation (I6), includes an eligible sample (I8), reports within-task regulation contrasts (I9), and provides group-level whole-brain analyses/peak coordinates (I10,I11). However, the emotional stimuli regulated/viewed are auditory (aversive/pleasant sounds) and monetary outcomes rather than visual stimuli; thus it fails Inclusion Criterion I7 (stimuli must be VISUAL). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I7 (stimulus modality).

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli (I5, I7), includes appropriate participant samples (I8), reports within-task contrasts of emotional viewing (NEG>NEU, POS>NEU) (I9), and performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with results/maps (I10,I11). However, the fMRI task did NOT instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy; it measured automatic/implicit regulation during passive viewing (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing instructions). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (required). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete. Conclusion: exclude because I6 is not met.

This study meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (faces) (I7), includes an appropriate participant sample including clinical and control groups (I8), and reports within-task contrasts of unregulated viewing (fearful > calm) suitable for inclusion (I9). The paper also reports whole-brain analyses and peak coordinates (I10) and presents results described in the text (I11). Although no emotion-regulation instruction was given (I6 not applicable), the meta-analysis objective explicitly allows studies that involve viewing without regulating; thus the study is eligible. No exclusion criteria are triggered: the paper includes whole-brain task activation maps (not only connectivity or ROI-only results), reports within-task effects, and is an empirical study. Full text appears complete, with methods, results, and discussion provided. Given the clear reporting of the fearful>calm contrast and whole-brain results, I include this study.

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal (reappraisal vs attend blocks) in adolescents during visual stimuli (photos of peers). It includes behavioral and neural analyses with the key within-task contrast (reappraisal > attend) and reports whole-brain group-level results with peak coordinates (right frontal pole, BA9/BA10) and cluster statistics. Both depressed and non-depressed groups are reported and compared. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical, includes whole-brain activation analyses (not only ROI or connectivity), reports within-task effects, and is not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation instructions. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of emotional faces in pediatric bipolar disorder and therefore meets several inclusion items (I5: task-based fMRI; I7: visual stimuli—faces; I8: eligible sample with patient and control groups; I9: within-task valence comparisons/contrasts (angry vs neutral); I11: results include tables of coordinates). However it does NOT meet key inclusion requirements: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy—participants performed a two-back working memory task with no reappraisal or other regulation instructions) and I10 (the paper does not report a conventional group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map/contrast; the reported peak coordinates derive from ICA functional-connectivity spatial maps rather than standard task activation contrasts). This study therefore falls under exclusion criterion E5 (reports connectivity-only analyses without accompanying whole-brain task activation maps). Because at least one exclusion criterion is met and important inclusion criteria are not satisfied, the study is excluded.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract and references provided). Abstract indicates a task-based fMRI study applying cognitive reappraisal (I5, I6 appear met). However, the abstract does not specify the sensory modality of stimuli (visualness not confirmed — I7 not met), does not report any within-task regulation contrasts (I9 not met), and does not report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps or peak coordinates (I10 not met). The study focuses on connectivity analysis methods (density-based k-means clustering vs ICA) and likely reports only connectivity results without whole-brain task activation maps, meeting exclusion E5. Because key information (stimulus modality, task contrasts, whole-brain activation results) is missing in the provided text, I exclude the study. Full text incomplete flag set; further review of the complete article could change this decision.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS pictures) and reports within-task regulation contrasts. The paper presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (thresholded Z maps) with peak coordinates in MNI space and extracts ROI activations; relevant contrasts (e.g., increase+decrease > view, increase>view, view>decrease) and behavioral ratings are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are referenced. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because stimuli are non-visual autobiographical memory recall (script-driven imagery), so the study does not meet inclusion criterion I7 (visual emotional stimuli). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation; cognitive reappraisal-like “analyze” strategy), I8 (sample eligible), I9 (reports within-task regulation contrasts), I10 (reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with standard-space coordinates), I11 (results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered by the full text. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation with whole-brain results and an appropriate sample (meets I5, I8, I9, I10, I11). However, it does NOT instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing instructions) and thus fails I6. Crucially, the emotional stimuli are words (drug and neutral words), not visual images/film/clips; the review excludes studies using word/sentence stimuli, so it fails I7. No exclusion criteria from E3–E7 apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it does not meet I6 and I7.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Reduce vs Maintain) of visual images in adolescents, includes a control group reported separately, reports the within-task contrast (Pre-Reduce vs Pre-Maintain; Reduce>Maintain as reappraisal success), and presents whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (voxelwise ANCOVA, cluster thresholds and reported clusters/coordinates). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The article is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use a cognitive reappraisal strategy (reinterpretation) to downregulate desire for visually presented food images. It reports within-task contrasts (REGULATE_TASTY > ADMIT_TASTY) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study (I5 and I10 satisfied) but does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review: (I6) participants were not instructed to use any emotion-regulation strategy — regulation was spontaneous/implicit rather than instructed; (I7) the emotional stimuli are interpersonal social interactions (Ultimatum Game offers and verbal negotiations), not standardized visual emotional stimuli (e.g., IAPS pictures, affective faces/scenes, or film clips); (I9) the analyses do not report within-task contrasts of instructed regulation (e.g., reappraise > look) or unregulated viewing contrasts of visual stimuli as defined by the review. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered by the manuscript. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Hence excluded for failing to meet I6, I7, and I9 while satisfying I5 and I10.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (faces/houses) and reports task contrasts (AF and IF) with within-group results and clinical/control samples. However, all second-level analyses are restricted to a priori ROIs and results are reported from ROI clusters (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map in standard space is provided). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI/small-volume-corrected results with no whole-brain analysis). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports within-task contrasts/unregulated viewing contrasts). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal; task is an implicit attention/interference task rather than instructed regulation) and I10 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation reported). Full text appears complete.

This study is a resting-state fMRI seed-based functional connectivity study in bipolar disorder, not a task-based emotion regulation experiment. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without any whole-brain task-evoked activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample qualifies: clinical and control groups reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not task-based fMRI), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation/cognitive reappraisal task), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli; resting state), I9 (no within-task regulation or viewing contrasts reported), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked group-level activation maps). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (fearful and neutral faces) and reports within-task contrasts of unregulated viewing (fearful > neutral) at the group level. Whole-brain group analyses with peak coordinates in standard space are reported. Sample includes a clinical PTSD group and traumatized controls reported separately. Although no instructed emotion-regulation strategy was used (I6 not met), the protocol and reported contrasts satisfy the meta-analysis objective by providing unregulated viewing contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text is complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (faces) with unregulated emotion vs control contrasts and whole-brain group analyses; however, it does NOT instruct any emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., cognitive reappraisal, distancing, acceptance) during the task. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (no instructed emotion regulation). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (detach vs permit), uses visual stimuli (IAPS/EmoPicS), includes within-task contrasts for emotion reactivity and regulation (e.g., permit negative > permit neutral; detach negative > permit negative), reports whole-brain exploratory analyses with results/tables, and uses an eligible sample. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; includes whole-brain task activation maps and within-task effects; not only connectivity or ROI-only). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (I5, I7). The sample is eligible (healthy adult participants; I8). The paper reports unregulated viewing contrasts (Disgust > Neutral, Fear > Neutral), fulfilling I9. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with thresholds and coordinates (random-effects analyses, ROI and exploratory whole-brain results), meeting I10 and I11. The study did not instruct an explicit emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met), but the meta-analysis objective permits inclusion of studies that simply view stimuli without regulating; thus lack of an instructed regulation condition does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) in which participants were explicitly instructed to use an emotion regulation strategy (“reality checking”) to down-regulate responses during presentation of negative emotional faces (I6). Stimuli are visual (static emotional faces) (I7). Sample is healthy adults with results reported at group level (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (contrast “view > regulate” and beta estimates used in repeated-measures ANOVA) (I9). Analyses include whole-brain GLM and report Talairach coordinates/peak locations in tables (I10) and these whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures (I11). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text is complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Overall, the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This study is excluded because it does not test instructed emotion regulation of visual emotional stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample acceptable), I10 (whole-brain group-level analyses reported), I11 (whole-brain results described in text/supplement). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy; task is a non-emotional Parametric Go/No-Go), I7 (stimuli are non-emotional letters, not visual emotional images/clips), I9 (no within-task contrast related to emotion regulation or unregulated emotional viewing; contrasts are cognitive control: Rejections, Commissions, Targets). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Full text appears complete.

Meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study with an instructed emotion-regulation paradigm (CBT-like reappraisal/reality-checking strategies), uses visual stimuli (IAPS images), reports results separately for MDD patients and matched controls, includes within-task contrasts (reduce vs attend, enhance vs attend), and presents whole-brain group-level analyses with reported cluster coordinates and tables/figures. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion (supplementary data noted but not required). No exclusion criteria are met.

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI experiment that instructed participants to regulate emotion (explicit 'Regulate' vs 'Look' instructions using cognitive-linguistic reappraisal strategies), used visual stimuli (static photographs of harsh faces and violent scenes), included both a clinical group (SAD) and a demographically-matched healthy control group with results reported separately, and presents within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (e.g. Regulate > Look; Look Harsh Face > Neutral) with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and peak coordinates in Talairach space. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (i.e., the full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study is task-based fMRI with visual stimuli and a suitable sample, and it reports trial-level task effects and relationships with behavior. However, it does NOT instruct participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraise/down-regulate instructions); instead it measures spontaneous expression of an emotion-regulation pattern, so inclusion criterion I6 (instructed regulation) is not met. Additionally, the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map with peak coordinates; analyses are ROI-based and pattern-expression based without reported whole-brain activation coordinates, violating exclusion criterion E4. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study employed resting-state fMRI connectivity during anticipation of a public speech and did not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses to visual stimuli. Inclusion met: I8 (sample: clinical group with separate control group reported). Inclusion NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation/cognitive reappraisal), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli; task-free/resting-state), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts reported), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only seed-based/resting-state connectivity analyses without any whole-brain task activation map). Therefore the study does not address the review objective and must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it uses resting-state fMRI and multivariate machine learning to classify PTSD subtypes rather than a task-based emotion regulation paradigm. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only resting-state analyses without any task-evoked whole-brain activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample: clinical and control groups reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli used; resting-state, eyes-closed), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or viewing contrasts reported), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked group-level task activation maps). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not address the review objective and must be excluded.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: none.
(b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: on-screen 'safe' vs 'shock' cues), I8 (eligible sample: clinical and control groups), I9 (reports within-task unregulated contrast: shock > safe and shock-I/II contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates), I11 (results reported in text/tables).
(c) Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instruction to participants to regulate or reappraise their emotional responses; the paradigm measured natural anticipatory fear without an instructed emotion-regulation strategy). Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for the regulation studies; it is excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual stimuli (images of high-fat/high-sugar foods; I7) with an eligible sample (young adults; I8). The paper reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., high-fat/sugar food > vegetables, high-fat/sugar food > water) and group analyses (I9). The authors explicitly state they used whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with thresholding (I10) and report results in the text/tables (I11). However, the fMRI tasks did NOT instruct participants to apply an emotion-regulation strategy during scanning: participants were asked to attend to pictures and were explicitly NOT asked to apply cognitive reappraisals (no instructed reappraisal condition), so inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation task) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet the mandatory I6 requirement.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive emotion regulation (detachment/distancing) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and other pictures). It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., permit > regulate, pF > rF) and group-level random-effects analyses with voxelwise results and MNI coordinates (amygdala maxima and other whole-brain activations described), meeting the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Sample is healthy adult females and behavioral/neural results are reported. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not only ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation).

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed cognitive reappraisal paradigm (Observe, Maintain, Suppress) with visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (Maintain>Observe; Suppress>Maintain) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and tables/figures. Both cocaine-dependent and control groups are reported separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing complete assessment. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that used a Stroop Match-to-Sample paradigm with emotional (angry face) visual stimuli and an instruction to ignore emotional interference (i.e., instructed cognitive control of emotional responses). The paper reports within-task contrasts (angry face > gray square), whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses with reported activations/coordinates, and seed-to-voxel functional connectivity; participants are adolescents including both an Internet gaming disorder group and healthy controls reported separately. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.
