No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, contains within-group task effects, and is not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation). Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a resting-state fMRI study (ALFF and seed-based rsFC) with no task, no instructed emotion-regulation paradigm, and no within-task contrasts or task-evoked activation maps. It therefore does not meet the review’s core inclusion requirements for a task-based emotion-regulation fMRI study. Exclusion criterion E5 applies because the paper reports only resting-state and connectivity/ALFF analyses without any whole-brain task activation maps. Inclusion criterion I8 (sample eligibility) is satisfied (older adult participants), but inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation task), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I9 (within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), and I10 (whole-brain task-evoked maps) are NOT met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion reason: The study does not provide a whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates (I10 not met) and primarily reports small-volume/ROI amygdala analyses and network-based functional connectivity (NBS). Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E4 (ROI/SVC results with no whole-brain activation maps) and E5 (connectivity-focused analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—faces), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (reports an unregulated viewing contrast: face-matching > form-matching). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation), I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level maps reported), and thus I11 (acceptable whole-brain reporting) is not applicable. Full text appears complete. Consequently the study is excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is a task-based, empirical fMRI study that directly instructs emotion regulation (‘decrease’ vs ‘attend’) using cognitive reappraisal-like instructions, with visual stimuli (photographs and IAPS images). The sample (n=16 after exclusions) is a healthy adult group. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g. decrease > attend, stigma > IAPS) and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (tables and figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not non-empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, and involves instructed regulation rather than mere perspective-taking). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion(s) met: E4 (study reports primarily ROI-based analyses with no group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps reported). Inclusion(s) met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (within-task contrast: unfair > fair, i.e. emotional/unregulated viewing contrast). Inclusion(s) NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy; participants reacted naturally to anger provocations rather than being instructed to reappraise/accept/distance/etc.), I7 (regulated stimuli are interactive social negotiations/offers with verbal provocations rather than visual-only stimuli such as images or film), I10 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates reported in standard space in this full text). Because the review requires an instructed emotion-regulation task and whole-brain task maps, this paper must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of frustration in children that includes whole-brain results, but it does not instruct participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing) or include an explicit regulation instruction. Therefore it fails the required criterion I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

Full text reviewed. Exclusion: none of the explicit exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample: healthy adults), I9 (reports within-task, unregulated viewing contrasts: self-critical > neutral, etc.), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation; participants were told to read words and attend to feelings, but were not instructed to reappraise or otherwise regulate), I7 (regulated/viewed stimuli are words/adjectives presented visually; the review excludes studies whose stimuli are word and sentence stimuli). Because two core inclusion criteria (I6 and I7) are not satisfied, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis despite being a task-based fMRI study with whole-brain results.

This study is a resting-state fMRI graph-theoretical connectivity study and does not include any task-based emotion regulation paradigm. Specifically, it uses resting-state scans (participants instructed to lie passively) and analyzes intrinsic functional connectivity/graph metrics; no instructed emotion regulation strategy, no visual emotional stimuli, no within-task regulation contrasts, and no task-evoked whole-brain activation maps are reported. Thus it fails key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Exclusion criterion E5 applies because the study reports only resting-state connectivity analyses without any whole-brain task activation results. The sample criterion is satisfied (I8: adult female participants), but the study does NOT meet I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I9 (within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), or I10 (whole-brain task-evoked maps). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study must be excluded. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 — the study reports only resting-state/ALFF analyses tied to pre/post cognitive tasks and does not report any whole-brain task-evoked activation maps for an emotion-regulation task. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I8 — sample criteria satisfied (older adults, clinical MCI and healthy controls reported separately). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 — not a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation (the fMRI was resting-state before/after tasks, not task-evoked fMRI); I6 — no instructed emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal/acceptance/other regulation instructions); I7 — emotional stimuli were not visual emotional images or films (affective response was to cognitive tasks, not visual emotional stimuli); I9 — no within-task contrast related to emotion regulation. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study in which children were instructed to use cognitive reappraisal ("MAKE-POSITIVE") to down-regulate negative responses to visual stimuli (I5, I6, I7). The sample includes clinical (MDD-ever) and healthy control groups reported separately, and the paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > view sad, view sad > view neutral) (I8, I9). However, the fMRI analyses are entirely ROI-based (amygdala subdivisions and 23 Diekhof ROIs); the manuscript does not report any group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps or whole-brain peak coordinates from a voxelwise analysis. Because the study reports only ROI analyses with no accompanying whole-brain voxelwise results, it violates exclusion criterion E4 and does not meet inclusion criterion I10. Therefore it must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (appraisal condition) using visual stimuli (faces and scenes). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (appraisal vs. implicit emotion processing), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard space. The sample (healthy adult males) is eligible. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11) and violates none.

The study is excluded because it does not instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met). It is a task-based fMRI study (I5 met), uses visual stimuli (colored squares) (I7 met), includes an eligible sample of healthy adults (I8 met), reports within-task contrasts (CS- > CS+ and CS+ > CS-) that qualify as unregulated viewing contrasts (I9 met), and provides group-level whole-brain task analyses with coordinates (I10 and I11 met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Because the review requires all inclusion criteria be met and this paper lacks instructed emotion regulation, it must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli with whole-brain analyses, but it does NOT instruct participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy (reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or explicit instructed regulation). Instead, the task manipulates attentional focus (Threat Focus vs Alternative Focus) and stimulus timing; these are attentional/goal-focus instructions rather than instructions to regulate or alter one’s emotional response. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion-regulation strategy) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task contrasts like threat>safe), I10 (whole-brain analyses with coordinates), I11 (results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal (reappraise vs view) with visual stimuli (IAPS images). Participants are adolescent girls (clinical PTSD sample) and analyses include within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraise > view; view negative > view neutral). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (task-modulated functional connectivity contrasts with clusterwise inference and reported clusters/figures; supplementary figures provide task activation maps), and results are reported with clusters/coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not between-group-only, not an empathy task). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

This is a task-based fMRI study using instructed cognitive reappraisal (REAL/PHOTO/LOOK cues) with visual stimuli (IAPS and photos). It reports within-task contrasts of reappraisal conditions (e.g., negative/real vs negative/photo) and whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected clusters and ROI analyses, and provides full methods, results, and discussion. The sample includes unmedicated MDD patients and healthy controls with separate reporting. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (film clips) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (negative > neutral; positive > neutral) with group-level, voxelwise whole-brain results (cluster-corrected, MNI coordinates). The sample (children and adults) is eligible. Although no explicit emotion regulation instructions were given (i.e., I6 not satisfied), the meta-analysis objective accepts unregulated viewing contrasts; the study therefore satisfies the necessary inclusion conditions for unregulated viewing studies. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an instructed antecedent-focused emotion regulation manipulation (precedent descriptions presenting images as fictitious vs real), fulfilling the review’s definition of extrinsic/incidental reappraisal. Stimuli were visual static images (mutilation/IAPS), participants were healthy adults, and the paper reports within-task contrasts (unpleasant > neutral) and ROI paired tests showing attenuation of amygdala/insula responses. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and coordinates/peaks are reported; standard group-level analyses were used. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual face stimuli that reports within-task contrasts (emotional face vs no-face) with peak coordinates and separate participant groups, so it meets I5, I7, I8, I9 and I11. However participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal/acceptance/etc. instructions)—the task required WM performance while ignoring emotional distracters—so I6 is not met. Analyses are restricted to ROI-based group tests (WFU PickAtlas masks and AlphaSim within ROIs) with no reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps, so I10 is not met. Because the paper reports only ROI results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis, exclusion criterion E4 applies. Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study is EXCLUDED. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample acceptable). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; participants were not told to reappraise or otherwise regulate emotion), I7 (stimuli were auditory tones and white-noise UCS, not VISUAL stimuli), I9 (no within-task contrast of instructed emotion regulation or an unregulated visual-viewing contrast as required), I10 (analyses were restricted to anatomical ROIs rather than reporting a whole-brain, voxelwise group map). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (results are reported using ROI-restricted analyses with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not satisfy the review objective of fMRI studies of instructed regulation or viewing of visual emotional stimuli.

Exclusion E4 applies: the study’s primary task activation results are reported using an a priori ROI (bilateral amygdala) rather than a group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates. Although a whole-brain PPI (connectivity) analysis is reported, the paper does not present a whole-brain voxelwise task-activation map (contrast of emotion viewing) with peaks in standard space. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: faces), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports an unregulated viewing contrast: fearful vs. happy). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy—the task was implicit gender discrimination, not reappraisal or other regulation), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map reported), I11 (no whole-brain activation peaks/tables provided). Because I10/I11 are not satisfied and the paper relies on ROI results without a whole-brain task activation map, it does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain task-evoked evidence and must be excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly addresses the review question. It uses an instructed emotion-regulation paradigm (LOOK/DECREASE) employing cognitive reappraisal instructions (I6) with visual stimuli from the IAPS (I7). The sample includes a clinical group (IGD) and matched controls reported separately (I8). Results include within-task effects (eg, negative vs neutral, look vs decrease; amygdala ROI and within-group comparisons) and contrasts related to regulation (I9). A group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM was conducted and reported with voxel-level thresholding and pFWE correction (voxel p<0.001, pFWE<0.05), with clusters reported in tables/figures (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper is empirical (not E3), reports whole-brain task activation (not E4 or E5), includes within-group task effects (not E6), and is not an empathy/perspective-taking study (not E7). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion regulation paradigm (enhance/suppress/attend) employing cognitive reappraisal strategies with visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., enhance conditions, sustained 2nd half vs 1st half) and voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses with peak coordinates in standard space (MNI). The sample includes depressed patients and healthy controls reported separately. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, includes whole-brain maps, includes within-group task effects, and is not an empathy/perspective-only task). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are noted but not required. Therefore, all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (faces) and an instructed emotion-labeling task (label > observe), with adolescent participants and within-task contrasts reported. However, the paper reports seed-based PPI connectivity focused on an a priori rVLPFC ROI and does not present a group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation map or peak coordinates in standard space. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I10 and meets exclusion criteria E5 (reports only seed-based/effective connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (ROI-restricted analysis without accompanying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I10. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (emotional faces) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., emotional face > fixation; happy/fearful vs. neutral). The sample (youth clinical and healthy controls) is eligible. The paper includes whole-brain (exploratory) group-level analyses (reported in supplemental Table S2) in standard space and provides coordinate-based results. Although the task did not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal instruction), the meta-analysis objective explicitly accepts unregulated viewing contrasts; therefore the study meets the review’s eligibility (task-based visual emotional stimuli with within-task contrasts and whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplements referenced).

This is a methods paper that applies a task-based fMRI dataset (threat vs safety cues; hand-holding conditions) and reports ROI-based voxelwise analyses. Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: threat/safety cues), I8 (sample reported), I9 (within-task contrasts such as threat > baseline and condition contrasts). Inclusion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as cognitive reappraisal; hand-holding is a social-context manipulation, not an instructed regulation strategy), I10 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps with peak coordinates reported; analyses were restricted to predefined ROIs). Exclusion applied: E4 (reports ROI-only results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Full text appears complete for screening.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which participants were instructed to use cognitive reappraisal (increase, maintain, decrease) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts of interest (increase/decrease > maintain) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (AUC images transformed to Talairach space, cluster correction via AlphaSim), with extracted cluster results. The sample (older adults) is acceptable. The full text supplied includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-visual/stimulus issues). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion rationale: No instructed emotion regulation during the fMRI task (participants completed a dispositional reappraisal questionnaire but were not instructed to reappraise), therefore inclusion criterion I6 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: aversive and neutral images), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (reports within-task unregulated contrast: aversive > neutral anticipation), I10 (reports whole-brain exploratory analysis with peak coordinates), I11 (whole-brain results clearly described). Exclusion criteria met: none. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I6 is not satisfied, the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (dynamic faces) with an unregulated viewing contrast (emotions vs. shapes) reported. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (FWE-corrected clusters) and provides region coordinates/cluster results. Sample includes clinical and healthy control groups. Although the task does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met), the study meets the meta-analysis’ allowance for unregulated viewing contrasts (I9). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it is eligible for inclusion under the unregulated viewing pathway.

Full text is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli and reports whole-brain, within-task contrasts, but it does NOT meet the required inclusion criterion I6: an instructed emotion-regulation strategy. The study examines implicit/spontaneous derogation (participants were not instructed to reappraise or otherwise regulate their emotions) and contrasts (reject>accept) reflect inferred, not instructed, regulation. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (within-task contrasts related to regulation/unregulated viewing), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinates), I11 (results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I6 (no instructed regulation). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED because it fails I6.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (angry and neutral faces) and reports an unregulated viewing contrast (Angry > Neutral) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and MNI peak coordinates. Sample is healthy adult participants. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Although no emotion-regulation instruction was given (I6 not met), the meta-analysis accepts unregulated viewing contrasts (I9), so the study addresses the review objective and meets the necessary inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (static facial photographs) and an implicit emotion-processing task (gender discrimination). The paper reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (angry>scrambled, fearful>scrambled, sad>scrambled, happy>scrambled, neutral>scrambled) and conducts group-level whole-brain analyses with reported clusters. Participant groups (MDD, Anx, DAC, HC) are reported separately. Although no emotion-regulation instructions were used, the review objective accepts unregulated viewing contrasts; thus the study meets the meta-analysis scope. Full text contains introduction, methods, analyses, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply.

Exclusion decision: The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual infant faces and reports whole-brain group results and coordinates, but it does NOT instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses (no reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other instructed regulation). Instead tasks are imitation and 'observe and try to empathize' (perspective-taking/empathy). This matches exclusion criterion E7 (empathy/perspective-taking studies with no instruction to amplify or dampen emotion). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: infant faces), I8 (sample qualifies: nulliparous adult females), I9 (reports within-task contrasts relevant to viewing: all faces>rest, emotional>neutral), I10 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses), I11 (coordinates/tables reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy). Therefore the paper should be excluded (E7). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) of remitted MDD patients and controls (I8) that reports group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinates (I10) and reports results in text/figures (I11). However, it does NOT instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing or other instructed emotion-regulation strategy), so it fails I6. The stimuli are letters and task-related visual feedback ('Too Slow'), not emotional visual stimuli such as IAPS pictures/faces/scenes or film clips, so it fails I7. The reported contrasts (error commission > correct hit, visual negative feedback > correct hit, and post-event contrasts) index executive/error processing and feedback, not within-task emotion-regulation contrasts (e.g. reappraise > look), so it fails I9. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study does not address the meta-analysis question of instructed emotion regulation of visual emotional stimuli and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to perform cognitive reappraisal (Decrease Negative, Increase Positive) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and supplemented images). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Decrease Negative vs Look Negative; Increase Positive vs Look Negative) and behavioral/ROI fMRI results. The authors also conducted a group-level voxelwise baseline functional localizer (negative vs neutral) using cluster correction and report region coordinates, which provides whole-brain task-evoked statistical mapping used to define ROIs. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical with original fMRI data, includes whole-brain voxelwise analysis (baseline localizer) and within-task contrasts, and does not rely solely on ROI-only or connectivity-only results. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal via distancing) in youth using visual stimuli (validated photographs), meeting the review’s core design. The paper reports within-task contrasts focused on regulation (Far) versus baseline and Far versus Look-Negative, and describes traditional univariate (GLM) whole-brain analyses with data registered to MNI152 and univariate results provided in the Supplement, satisfying the requirement for group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps/coordinates. The sample (typically developing children/adolescents) is eligible. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity-only analyses, non-empirical work) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary univariate results are referenced. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is a task-based fMRI RCT of instructed cognitive reappraisal with appropriate analyses, whole-brain results, and suitable sample (meets I5, I6, I8, I9, I10, I11). However, the regulated stimuli are participant-generated autobiographical situations and negative self-beliefs presented as sentences/text (word/sentence stimuli), not visual images or film clips, so inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli) is NOT met. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study must be excluded.

Full-text report describes an event-related, task-based fMRI study using the SEAT paradigm with instructed emotion modulation (appraisal 'Like/Dislike' and attentional modulation conditions). Stimuli are visual (faces and scenes). The paper reports within-task condition effects (implicit emotion processing vs baseline and condition-specific simple effects), and group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with peak MNI coordinates and FWE correction. The report includes methods, results, and discussion (full article content present). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-task effects).

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs participants to use an attention-to-breath (ATB) mindfulness regulation strategy during presentation of aversive visual stimuli (IAPS). It reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation and passive viewing ([ATB vs PV], [PV vs ATB], picture vs no-picture), and links brain activation to behavioral regulation success. Whole-brain group-level analyses are reported (cluster/FWE thresholds) alongside ROI analyses and coordinate-based results. Sample is healthy adult participants and analyses include emotion-related contrasts and PPI connectivity but also whole-brain task activation maps. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present and sufficient for screening.

This study is an fMRI task study of pain controllability but does not meet key eligibility requirements for this review. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I11 (results reported as coordinates/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; participants were allowed to stop pain but were not instructed to perform cognitive reappraisal or another directed regulation strategy), I7 (regulated stimuli are somatosensory electrical pain, not VISUAL stimuli), I9 (the within-task contrasts pertain to controllability/analgesia rather than an instructed emotion-regulation vs view contrast). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because it does not involve instructed regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs cognitive reappraisal (reduce vs. maintain) as the emotion-regulation strategy (I6); stimuli are visual static pictures from the Native Chinese Affective Picture System (I7); participants are healthy adult volunteers (I8); the paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (reduce vs. maintain) (I9); analyses include group-level whole-brain voxelwise tests with reported peak coordinates and FDR correction (I10), and results/coordinates are clearly described in the text (I11). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (appears complete).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal while participants view visual images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > look), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with thresholding and tables/figures of activations, and provides full methods, results and discussion. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual IAPS stimuli and whole-brain group analyses reporting unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., expectation/presentation negative > neutral). However, the study does not instruct participants to use any emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, or other instructed regulation during anticipation or stimulus). They only assessed habitual regulation via ERQ post-scan. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation) is not met, so the study is excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI experiment (patients with generalized SAD) that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal (‘Reframe’ vs ‘Just Watch’) while participants viewed dynamic visual social evaluation video clips. Emotional stimuli are visual (video clips). The authors report within-task contrasts (react and reappraise trials versus asterisk baseline; reappraise vs react examined in connectivity) and test pre-to-post treatment changes. Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level random-effects maps with Talairach-space results and cluster-correction; peak coordinates and cluster statistics are reported. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not a non-empirical paper, and task includes instructed regulation rather than mere perspective-taking). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI empirical study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) and includes an instructed reappraisal task in the scanner (participants were trained and then applied reappraisal in an instructed task), as well as an uninstructed negative image viewing task whose activation estimates are analyzed. Sample (adult participants) meets inclusion. The paper reports within-task activation estimates for stimulus viewing and a group-level whole-brain analysis with peak coordinates (e.g., vlPFC, dlPFC, dmPFC clusters), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Thus it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (includes instructed emotion regulation task), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample), I9 (reports within-task activation related to viewing/regulation), I10 (group-level whole-brain maps with coordinates), and I11 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal) using visual stimuli (IAPS images) in patients with MDD and matched controls, with within-task contrasts (negative decrease > negative look) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses reported (including Talairach coordinates and cluster-thresholded maps). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and it reports within-task effects). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This study is excluded because it reports only resting-state fMRI and structural MRI data without any task-based emotion regulation or visual-stimulus viewing paradigm. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports ONLY resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample: includes clinical participant groups). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli presented), I9 (no within-task regulation or viewing contrasts reported), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked group-level activation maps). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study is excluded because it fails inclusion criterion I7: the emotional stimuli regulated are internally-generated autobiographical memories (imagery), not visual stimuli (e.g., pictures, films, faces). It does meet several other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation task to upregulate positive emotion via autobiographical recall), I8 (healthy adult sample reported), I9 (reports within-task contrasts such as train>rest and happy>rest), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates), and I11 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because the meta-analysis requires regulated stimuli to be visual and this study uses non-visual, internally-driven stimuli, it does not satisfy all inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (faces) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and within-task contrasts of emotional viewing (e.g., fear > calm, early > late habituation). Thus it meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. However, participants were not instructed to use any emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance); the task required detection/response suppression but did not instruct subjects to regulate their emotional responses. Therefore it does NOT meet I6 (an instructed emotion regulation strategy) and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text appears complete.

Full text reports an empirical task-based fMRI study in which participants were instructed to use a cognitive reappraisal strategy (detachment) to regulate emotions elicited by visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). Methods and results include within-task contrasts of regulation versus no-regulation (e.g., negative regulation > no regulation), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with corrected thresholds and peak coordinates, and separate patient and healthy control group reporting. The paper also reports psychophysiological interaction analyses but not as the sole analysis. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I11) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (face-matching) with a within-task unregulated viewing contrast (emotion > shape). It provides group-level whole-brain statistical maps, tables/figures, and coordinates, and includes complete methods, results, and discussion. It therefore meets: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—faces), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrast emotion > shape), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps with coordinates), and I11 (results clearly described in text/tables/figures). The study did not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met), but the meta-analysis objective explicitly accepts unregulated viewing contrasts; thus inclusion is appropriate. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and reports within-task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (Decrease) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images), meeting the review objective. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. Negative Decrease vs Negative Look; Neutral Decrease vs Neutral Look) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI peak coordinates and cluster-based correction. Both bipolar patients and healthy controls are included and reported separately. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical paper). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and the study should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (Think Positive / Think Negative) during presentation of visual stimuli (static face images). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Enhance Positive > Pre-Regulation; Enhance Negative > Pre-Regulation; regulation > pre) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster tables and figures (FDR-thresholded results reported). Both ASD and control groups are included and control results are reported separately. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the report appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task effects, not an empathy-only task). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This study fails inclusion criterion I7. Although it is a task-based fMRI RCT (I5) with an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (observe/attention regulation; I6), includes a clinical SAD sample (I8), reports within-task regulation contrasts (regulate vs react; I9), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates (I10) and coordinate tables described in text (I11), the regulated stimuli are participant-generated autobiographical descriptions and negative self-belief sentences presented as written words/sentences on the screen. The review’s eligibility rules explicitly exclude studies whose regulated stimuli are word/sentence stimuli. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are otherwise met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude due to not meeting I7.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation (I5) using visual stimuli (animated Cyberball; I7) in an adolescent sample (I8). It reports within-task contrasts of unregulated viewing (observed inclusion vs observed exclusion; I9) and presents whole-brain, group-level results with peak coordinates and tables (I10, I11). However, the study did NOT instruct participants to use any emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other instructed regulation), so it fails inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) appear to be met. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I6 is not met, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (“realize being safe”) during presentation of visual social images (IAPS and additional erotic images). The paper reports within-task contrasts of regulation (negative-safe versus negative-look) and unregulated viewing (negative-look versus neutral-look), and conducts group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with reported cluster coordinates. Participants include clinical (BPD and cluster-C) and nonpatient control groups reported separately. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Summary: This is a task-based fMRI study of mindfulness/MBCT in bipolar patients that instructs an acceptance/open-awareness strategy and reports within-task contrasts (meditate > control) and whole-brain voxelwise group analyses with peak coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation-like strategy: acceptance/open awareness), I8 (clinical sample with control group), I9 (reports within-task contrasts related to the instructed regulation task), I10 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with coordinates). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 — the emotional stimuli are not visual; the task involved internal mindfulness/meditation without presentation of visual emotional images or film clips, whereas the meta-analysis requires regulation or viewing of visual emotional stimuli. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Full text appears complete.

Although this is a task-based, within-subject fMRI study reporting whole-brain task activation maps and coordinates, it fails the review's stimulus criterion. The regulated emotional stimuli are experimenter-selected negative self-belief sentences (word/sentence stimuli presented on screen). The meta-analysis exclusion explicitly excludes studies whose regulated stimuli are word/sentence stimuli (I7 not met). Other inclusion criteria are satisfied (see list). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed cognitive reappraisal (‘distance’) and ‘immerse’ conditions using visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to the review (distance/aversive > immerse/aversive; immerse/aversive > immerse/neutral) and provides group-level whole-brain analyses with MNI coordinates. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli in bipolar patients and healthy controls, and it reports event-related responses to negative pictures (so I5, I7, I8, I9 are met). However, participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses (no reappraisal, acceptance, distancing, cue-based regulation, etc.), so I6 is not met. Analyses focus on ROI-extracted percent signal change (OFC, amygdala, other ROIs) and do not report a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map with peak coordinates; thus I10 is not met and exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI results with no whole-brain analysis) applies. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Because the review requires an instructed emotion-regulation task and/or whole-brain task activation maps, this study does not satisfy all inclusion criteria and is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a fear conditioning/extinction paradigm with visual stimuli and whole-brain voxelwise analyses. However, participants were not instructed to employ an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing); the task probes unregulated conditioned fear and extinction. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation task) is not met, so the study does not match the meta-analysis requirement. Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal (increase/decrease) while viewing visual IAPS images. The sample (young adults) is acceptable. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g. decrease-negative > view-neutral), provides second-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and cluster tables, and includes methods, results, and discussion in full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual IAPS pictures, with patient and healthy control groups and within-task contrasts (e.g. negative > neutral), so it meets I5, I7, I8, and I9. However, participants were instructed to anticipate and view stimuli rather than to use an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met). Critically, the fMRI analysis was a hypothesis-driven ROI analysis (predefined spherical ROIs) and the paper reports ROI beta-weights rather than group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps or peak coordinates; thus it fails I10 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI results, no whole-brain analysis). Because E4 is met and key inclusion criteria (I6 and I10) are not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Provided content includes only article metadata (title, authors, journal, DOI) and not the full text (methods, results). Therefore fulltext_incomplete=true and I cannot verify required criteria. Based on title, the study likely used fMRI neurofeedback so inclusion I5 (task-based fMRI) is plausibly met. However there is no information confirming: I6 (instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I9 (within-task emotion-regulation or viewing contrasts), or I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps with coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E3-E7) are clearly met from the available metadata. Conclusion: EXCLUDED due to incomplete full text preventing verification of core inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I9, I10).

This is an EEG/ERP study of neural responses to emotional faces in clinically anxious children using a go/no-go task. It is empirical and reports stimulus- and response-locked ERP contrasts across emotion and trial types. However, it is not an fMRI study (does not use task-based fMRI or report whole-brain voxelwise maps), and participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing or other instructed regulation strategy). Consequently, key inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis are not met. Inclusion criteria met: visual stimuli (faces) and eligible sample (children with clinical and comparison groups). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation), I9 (within-task regulation contrast), and I10 (whole-brain fMRI results/coordinates). No exclusion criteria from the review’s list (E3–E7) specifically apply. Full text appears complete for the EEG study but does not meet fMRI/regulation-focused inclusion requirements.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual emotional images and reports whole-brain group-level contrasts (negative > neutral) with coordinates, but the fMRI task did not instruct participants to use any emotion regulation strategy (it was an emotion identification/discrimination task). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (no instructed regulation), though it meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that presents visual emotional stimuli (film clips) and reports within-task contrasts comparing negative vs neutral clips (unregulated viewing). The paper includes group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results with reported clusters/peaks (tables/figures) and supplementary material. Although participants were not instructed to use an explicit regulation strategy (I6 not met), the review’s inclusion allows unregulated viewing contrasts (I9), which this study provides. Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis requirements and should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study of passive viewing of visual emotional stimuli (movie clips of fearful and neutral faces) with a clear within-task unregulated viewing contrast (negative > neutral). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (cluster-level FWE-corrected results with peak activations reported), and includes separate patient (BPD) and healthy control groups. Stimuli are visual; behavioural and imaging analyses include the relevant contrasts. Although no emotion-regulation instruction was given (i.e., I6 not met), the study provides an unregulated viewing contrast that satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion (I9). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion; supplemental material is not required. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which children passively viewed visual emotional stimuli (faces) and task-evoked activations were reported. The study reports unregulated viewing contrasts (face conditions vs. fixation/baseline and emotion effects), whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster thresholds and reported regional effects, and peak/cluster results consistent with standard reporting. The sample (4–6-year-old clinical and control groups) is eligible. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given (no reappraisal/down-regulation task), the review protocol accepts unregulated viewing contrasts (I9), so the study fits the meta-analysis objective of including viewing-only studies. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the report appears complete.

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI study in PTSD patients that includes an instructed emotion regulation (Reappraisal) task (Decrease/Reappraise vs Look), uses visual stimuli (IAPS pictures and face images), and reports within-task contrasts such as Reappraise Negative > Look Negative and Look Negative > Neutral. The paper describes voxel-wise, group-level linear mixed-effects (task-evoked) analyses and refers to supplemental tables/figures with coordinate results, satisfying the whole-brain reporting requirement. The sample (clinical PTSD) is eligible and results include both regulation and unregulated viewing contrasts. The article contains full introduction, methods, results, and discussion (supplemental materials referenced but not required). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

All inclusion criteria are met: this is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal; I6). Stimuli are visual negative IAPS images (I7). The sample is a clinical group (panic disorder) which is acceptable (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation and unregulated viewing (e.g. Reappraisal > Maintain, Maintain > Reappraisal, images > baseline) (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise with thresholding and reported MNI coordinates (I10), and results are clearly described in the text with coordinate details (I11). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, includes whole-brain analyses, not only connectivity, includes within-group task effects, and is not an empathy/perspective-taking study). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The full text reports a task-based fMRI randomized trial using an instructed cognitive reappraisal emotion regulation task (ERT) and an emotion perception task (EFAT) with visual stimuli (IAPS images and facial expressions). It includes clinical participants (anxiety/depression), reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation and viewing (Reappraise Negative vs. Look Negative; Look Negative vs. Look Neutral; Emotional Faces vs. Shapes), and describes whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (FDR-corrected) with whole-brain results referenced in Supplementary Materials. The article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the meta-analysis’s task-based fMRI and emotion-regulation criteria. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (study reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses without any whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample qualifies: adolescent participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation task/cognitive reappraisal), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli presented during fMRI task), I9 (no within-task regulation or viewing task contrasts reported), I10 (no whole-brain, task-evoked group-level activation maps). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is excluded because it does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the review. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual stimuli (I7), includes clinical and control groups (I8), and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts of emotional pictures (I9). However, the task involved passive viewing without any instructed emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, cue/anticipation regulation, etc.), so I6 is not met. Analyses are restricted to an a priori amygdala ROI (mean % activation) and the paper does not report a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical map or peak coordinates in standard space, so I10 is not met. Because only ROI results are reported, exclusion criterion E4 applies. Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of masked visual emotional faces in chronic marijuana smokers and controls (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11). However, it does not instruct participants to use any emotion regulation strategy; subjects performed gender discrimination and passively viewed masked affective stimuli, with no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing or other instructed regulation (violates I6). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 (emotion-regulation instruction).

This full text meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using an instructed emotion regulation paradigm with cognitive reappraisal instructions (‘reappraise…so it elicits less negative affect’) (I6). Emotional stimuli are visual pictures (fear and OCD-related images) (I7). The sample includes OCD patients and demographically matched healthy controls with results reported for groups (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (fear regulate > attend; OCD-related regulate > attend) (I9). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are performed and peak coordinates are reported in MNI space (figures/tables/text) (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references).

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation that explicitly instructed participants to regulate negative emotions (increase/decrease) after errors and reports within-task regulation contrasts and whole-brain coordinates; however, it does not examine regulation of emotional responses to visual affective stimuli (I7). The emotion that is regulated is internally generated by error commission during a cognitive task rather than being evoked by visual emotional images/films/facial expressions. Therefore it does not match the meta-analysis requirement that the regulated stimuli be visual emotional stimuli. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered by the full text. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criterion not met: I7.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (child faces) and reports whole-brain analyses with MNI coordinates. However, the meta-analysis requires studies that instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, acceptance) and report within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look) or unregulated viewing contrasts (emotion > baseline). This study uses an emotional conflict task (incongruent vs. congruent) and participants performed face/gender or emotion labeling; they were not instructed to regulate or reappraise their emotional responses. Therefore key inclusion criteria I6 (instructed emotion regulation) and I9 (within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrast relevant to emotion regulation) are not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a visual face-matching paradigm (faces vs shapes) that provides within-task contrasts isolating emotional processing and reports group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses with peak coordinates. The sample includes bipolar patients and healthy controls with results reported separately. Although the task probes implicit emotional processing rather than an instructed regulation strategy, the meta-analysis accepts both regulation and unregulated viewing studies; thus the study meets the review objective and relevant inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual IAPS pictures (I7). The task explicitly instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (voluntary attentional regulation: shape-evaluation vs valence-evaluation), meeting the instructed regulation criterion (I6). The sample includes MDD patients and healthy controls with results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts tied to regulation (SRT vs ERT and valence contrasts) (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM second-level tests with voxelwise and cluster-FWE thresholds and extraction of local activation peaks (I10); results/coordinates are described and supplemental tables are referenced (I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and within-group effects are reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation that instructs participants to exert cognitive control over emotional visual distractors (ignore emotional face distractors) during an N-back working memory task, which qualifies as instructed cognitive control of an emotional response. Stimuli are visual (faces). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotional processing (fearful>neutral; happy>neutral) and an interaction contrast linking emotional distractors with working-memory load, and conducts whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with reported significant clusters (e.g., left IFG BA45). The sample includes a clinical group (schizophrenia) and healthy controls with results reported separately. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Excluded because the study does not meet key stimulus and task requirements for this meta-analysis. The emotional stimuli were auditory/script-driven stories (non-visual), violating inclusion I7 (visual stimuli required). Participants were instructed to take the protagonist’s perspective during listening (perspective-taking) with no instruction to amplify or dampen their own emotional response, which matches exclusion E7 (perspective-taking studies without regulation). The study does meet several other criteria (I5: task-based fMRI; I8: eligible sample including controls; I9: reports within-task emotion contrasts, e.g., anger > neutral; I10: group-level whole-brain analyses reported; I11: results presented in text/figures). However, it does not satisfy I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy) and I7 (stimuli non-visual). Given these violations, the study must be excluded.

This article is a study protocol/design paper without empirical task-based fMRI group results necessary for this meta-analysis. Exclusion E3 applies because no original group-level fMRI outcome data are reported. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI design), I7 (visual stimuli: faces/visual objects), I8 (sample includes children/adolescents), I9 (within-task contrasts are planned: winning vs frustration, neutral vs emotional faces, correct vs incorrect Go trials). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal; the task induces frustration and measures spontaneous/regulatory processes but does not instruct participants to reappraise or otherwise regulate), and I10 (no reported group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps with peak coordinates; only planned/illustrative single-subject example is shown). Because both a lack of instructed regulation (I6) and absence of reported whole-brain group results (I10), plus the paper being non-empirical in terms of task-fMRI outcomes, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the study does not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing instruction) and thus does not meet the emotion-regulation task requirement. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI) and I8 (sample qualifies). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy), I7 (regulated stimuli are written statements/sentences rather than the visual image/video stimuli specified), I9 (no within-task contrast of regulation vs. view; contrasts are illness vs. control evaluations, not regulation contrasts), and I10 (no clearly reported whole-brain, group-level task activation map surviving whole-brain correction; reported results rely on small-volume/ROI corrections). Exclusion criterion met: E4 (results are reported with small-volume corrections/ROIs rather than whole-brain-corrected findings). Therefore the study does not satisfy the review’s core inclusion requirements and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (static faces) (I7) in an eligible sample (children/adolescents; clinical high-risk group with healthy controls reported separately) (I8). The paper reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (face > shape) (I9) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses normalized to Talairach space with cluster-level results (I10, I11). Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given (I6 not applicable), the meta-analysis objective explicitly allows studies that involve unregulated viewing of visual emotional stimuli, and the study therefore meets the required criteria for inclusion. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli and an instructed cognitive-control task (EFNBACK) with appropriate within-task contrasts (e.g., emotional-distracter vs. no-distracter) and reported MNI peak coordinates, the reported activation results are restricted to predefined ROIs with ROI-based multiple-comparison correction (AlphaSim) and PPI analyses constrained to target ROIs. The paper does not present or report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or whole-brain coordinates outside ROI-restricted results. This meets exclusion criterion E4 (ROI-only results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive control of emotional response via ignoring emotional distracters), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (within-task contrasts reported), and I11 (coordinates reported for ROI clusters). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked group map reported). Consequently the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (faces) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (emotional faces > shapes) as well as whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates (amygdala xyz reported; supplementary material referenced). Participant sample (SAD patients) is acceptable. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given, the review objective includes studies that simply view emotional stimuli without regulating, and the paper reports the necessary within-task contrasts. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for unregulated viewing contrasts and provides whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) and reports within-task contrasts comparing emotional trials to geometrical trials (unregulated viewing contrasts), with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected) and separate reporting for patients and controls. The sample and methods are fully reported. Thus it satisfies I5 (task fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample), I9 (within-task emotion-related contrasts – unregulated viewing), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise results), and I11 (results reported in text/supplement). The study does not instruct an explicit emotion-regulation strategy (I6), but the meta-analysis objective explicitly allows inclusion of studies that view emotional stimuli without regulating; therefore the study is eligible as an unregulated viewing task. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based (rtfMRI) experimental study that instructed participants to volitionally regulate anterior insula activity using an instructed strategy (recalling/imagining negative personal events) and then presented visual emotional stimuli (painful pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts (regulation > baseline), whole-brain group-level activation maps with MNI coordinates and appropriate corrections, and includes full methods, results, and discussion. Sample and analyses meet inclusion requirements. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study instructing participants to down-regulate their emotional response to visual (aversive) pictures, and it reports within-task contrasts (e.g. 'regulate>view'). However, the reported task results are presented primarily using region-of-interest analyses and small-volume corrections (amygdala and a vmPFC ROI). The paper does not present a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates in standard space that would qualify as a whole-brain task result. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I10 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI/SVC results with no accompanying whole-brain task analysis).

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed affect-labeling task (affect label vs gender label), an incidental emotion regulation strategy applied to visual stimuli (photographs of faces). The paper reports within-task contrasts and pre/post treatment paired analyses, whole-brain PPI and activation results with peak MNI coordinates and cluster-level correction, and separates reports for SAD and healthy control groups. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete.

Exclusion E4 applies: the paper reports only ROI-masked group analyses (region-of-interest/full-factorial within an a priori relapse mask) and does not present a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI with cue-exposure paradigms), I7 (visual stimuli: alcohol and neutral images), I8 (clinical sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task contrast alcohol > neutral). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy; passive cue-reactivity, not reappraisal or other instructed regulation), I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise group analysis reported). Full text appears complete. Thus excluded because it fails I6 and I10 and meets exclusion E4.

This study is a resting-state, seed-based connectivity fMRI investigation in adolescent marijuana users and does not involve a task or instructed emotion regulation. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (reports ONLY seed-based connectivity/resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample includes adolescents). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation/cognitive reappraisal), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli/task; resting-state), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps reported), I11 (not applicable as whole-brain task results are absent). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not address the review objective and must be excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to regulate emotion (explicit ‘regulate’ vs ‘view’ cues), using visual stimuli (IAPS and photographs). The paper reports within-task contrasts (regulate negative > view negative; regulate positive > view positive), group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported MNI peak coordinates and thresholds, and also provides results in the text/tables. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I11 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-task effects).

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were explicitly instructed to regulate emotion (distancing/taking the position of a noninvolved observer) versus naturally experiencing emotions while viewing visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The paper includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates and correction procedures (FDR whole-brain, FWE within ROIs), within-task contrasts related to regulation and unregulated viewing, and detailed methods, results, and discussion. Sample (healthy adults) is eligible. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, non-empirical, connectivity-only, or non-regulation perspective-taking without emotion regulation) are met. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore this study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Excluded based on E5: the paper reports task-modulated seed-based connectivity (gPPI) results and prediction analyses but does not report any whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation maps (univariate activation contrasts) with peak coordinates in standard space. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (explicit emotion regulation instruction — positive upregulation), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS and neutral images), I8 (clinical sample with controls reported separately), I9 (within-task contrast used: Positive Increase > Positive View). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported). Because E5 (reports ONLY seed-based connectivity without also reporting a whole-brain task activation map) is met, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study is a resting-state fMRI investigation of network connectivity in mTBI patients; it does not involve a task-based emotion regulation paradigm or instructed regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample: clinical participants reported separately). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not task-based fMRI), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli; resting-state only), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked activation maps reported). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only resting-state analyses without any task activation maps). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not address the review objective and must be excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs participants to use a cognitive emotion-regulation strategy (positive reappraisal) during the Picture Viewing Task (I6). The regulated stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7). The sample (clinical participants; transdiagnostic emotional distress disorders) is acceptable (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Positive Reappraisal vs Negative Attend) and relates activation to behavior (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps using FSL/FLAME with cluster correction and reported results/tables and supplemental figures (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, and it is not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore include for the meta-analysis.

Although this is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual emotional face stimuli in a healthy adult sample and reports group-level whole-brain results with peak coordinates, it does NOT instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (e.g. reappraisal, distancing, acceptance) and therefore fails inclusion criterion I6. The reported within-task contrasts (affect-incongruent > congruent in an approach–avoidance task) index voluntary control of action tendencies rather than an instructed emotion-regulation manipulation; thus it does not meet I9 (within-task contrast specifically related to instructed emotion regulation or an unregulated viewing contrast). Full text appears complete. Inclusion IDs met: I5, I7, I8, I10, I11. Inclusion IDs not met: I6, I9. No exclusion criteria from the list apply.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal Reduce vs Maintain; I6), uses visual stimuli (IAPS images; I7), includes adolescents with MDD and matched healthy controls with control results reported separately (I8), reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Maintain vs Reduce, Reduce vs Maintain; I9), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected cluster thresholds and coordinate-based reporting plus ROI analyses (I10). Reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables meets I11. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are violated. Therefore include.

Excluded because the fMRI task did not involve an instructed emotion regulation strategy (inclusion criterion I6 not met). The study used a face–word emotional conflict task that measures implicit emotion conflict adaptation rather than an instructed regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: faces), I8 (eligible sample: older adults), I9 (reports within-task contrast related to emotion regulation: iI vs cI), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E7 applicable). Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

Excluded because the fMRI task did not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (instructed regulation criterion I6 not met) and the reported fMRI results are reported using small-volume correction/ROI analyses (amygdala SVC) with no accompanying whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map reported, thus violating exclusion criterion E4. The study does meet several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli — faces), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts, e.g., faces > baseline), and I11 (coordinates/results reported in text). However it fails I6 (no instructed regulation) and I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise group map). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an emotion label vs match task (implicit emotion regulation). Participants were instructed to label emotions (an instructed task that engages implicit emotion regulation), using visual stimuli (facial expressions). The paper reports within-task contrasts (emotion label > emotion match), whole-brain group-level analyses with cluster thresholds and MNI peak coordinates, and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Sample (early-adolescent participants) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of visual emotional stimuli (sad vs neutral faces) in patient and control groups and reports within-task contrasts (sad>neutral). However, all reported neuroimaging results are ROI-based (amygdala, ventromedial and ventrolateral PFC) with percent signal change extracted using MarsBaR; no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical maps or peak coordinates in standard space are reported. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports ONLY region-of-interest results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (acceptable sample), and I9 (reports an unregulated viewing contrast: sad > neutral).
