Inclusion criteria not met: I10 (no whole-brain group-level task-evoked map reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to regulate their emotional responses (up- and down-regulate) to visual negative pictures with real-time amygdala neurofeedback. The paper reports within-task contrasts (up vs down; up vs view; down vs view) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with coordinates and corrected cluster results. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for task-based emotion regulation fMRI with visual stimuli and provides whole-brain activation evidence.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (Decrease Negative, Increase Negative) and other instructed regulation strategies. Stimuli are visual IAPS images (static pictures). The sample includes both an MDD patient group and a healthy control group with separate group-level analyses. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Decrease Negative > Look Negative; Increase Negative > Look Neutral) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task effects, not an empathy/perspective-only task). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. Accordingly, all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in an eligible sample and reports an unregulated viewing contrast (NEG–NEU) with peak coordinates, it does NOT meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. The fMRI task presented words (visual word stimuli) rather than images or videos, and the manuscript does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal/regulated > unregulated contrast). Thus it fails I6 (no instructed emotion regulation) and I7 (stimuli are words, which the protocol excludes). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly tests instructed cognitive reappraisal (enhance vs. suppress) using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (enhance–suppress) for the emotion regulation fMRI session, conducts whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (FLAME) with cluster correction, and reports peak coordinates in MNI space (Tables and figures). Participant sample is a healthy group of males (acceptable per I8). Thus all required inclusion criteria for the review are met (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not non-empirical, does not report only ROI or connectivity results, and includes within-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Recommendation: INCLUDE in the meta-analysis. If desired, extract the reported whole-brain peak coordinates (Tables 1 & 2) and the (enhance> suppress) contrasts for coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This is an empathy-focused task fMRI study without any instructed emotion regulation (no reappraisal/distancing/other regulation instructions). Although it reports task-evoked whole-brain visual stimulus activations, it does not instruct participants to amplify or dampen their own emotional responses; thus it meets exclusion E7. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli used for ER and EPT tasks), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts/task-evoked activations), I10 (whole-brain analyses reported), I11 (results reported in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The full text is complete but the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (faces) with reported within-task unregulated viewing contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results; however, the task did not instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal/distancing/acceptance instruction)—participants simply viewed emotional faces and performed an attention button-press. Therefore I6 (instruction of an emotion regulation strategy) is not met, while I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (static facial expressions) (I7). Participants were explicitly instructed to try to become as happy or sad as possible using the faces (an instructed up-regulation/generation strategy), which meets the requirement for an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (I6) and/or qualifies for up-/down-regulation contrasts. The paper reports within-task contrasts of emotion versus baseline (sadness > baseline; happiness > baseline), satisfying the requirement for a within-task emotion regulation or unregulated viewing contrast (I9). Analyses were performed as group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise SPM2 analyses with cluster reporting and anatomical labeling (whole-brain task-evoked maps) consistent with I10; results are described and clusters reported in the text/tables (I11). The full text includes methods, results and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-task effects). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Specifically: (a) inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample acceptable — clinical and control groups reported), I9 (within-task contrasts reported: anger>baseline, aggression>baseline), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates reported), I11 (coordinates/tables described in text/supplement). (b) inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 — no instructed emotion-regulation strategy (participants were instructed to imagine scenes, not to reappraise, distance, accept, or otherwise regulate); I7 — stimuli are non-visual (script-driven auditory narratives with imagination rather than visual images/video). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude for failing the required regulation instruction and visual-stimulus criteria.

This full text reports an empirical, task-based fMRI study in children with visual emotional stimuli and within-task contrasts (fearful faces during Winning vs Recovery). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: faces/objects), I8 (sample: children included), I9 (reports within-task contrast related to emotional context: Winning > Recovery for fearful-face events), and I10 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported). However, it fails the key inclusion criterion I6: participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (no instructed reappraisal or other explicit regulation instruction); the authors explicitly note there was no condition with explicit regulation instruction. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I6) and must be excluded.

Exclusion: E5 applies — the study reports resting-state and seed-based functional connectivity analyses (amygdala connectivity) and does not provide a whole-brain task-evoked activation map relevant to instructed emotion regulation. Inclusion: I8 is satisfied (sample characteristics: female clinical BPD group and healthy controls reported separately). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal/distancing was employed), I7 (regulated stimuli are not visual emotional images; stress was induced via the Montreal Imaging Stress Task and incision, not visual emotional stimuli), I9 (no within-task contrast reflecting emotion regulation like “reappraise > look”), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map reported), and I5 (while an fMRI task was used for stress induction, the study does not constitute a task-based emotion-regulation fMRI study as required by the review objective). Full text appears complete.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI experiment that explicitly instructs emotion regulation (cognitive downregulation) during viewing of visual emotional stimuli (film clips). The methods describe within-task contrasts (Regulate vs Attend), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space (tables and whole-brain results reported), and ROI analyses; participants are healthy adults and results include within-group and between-group effects. These elements satisfy all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is complete. The study is a task-based fMRI study of the Ultimatum Game with visual stimuli (faces) and reports whole-brain unfair>fair contrasts. However, it does not instruct participants to use any emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance); participants simply decide to accept or reject offers. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (regulated emotion strategy instructed). It meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task contrast unfair>fair reported), I10 (whole-brain analyses reported), and I11 (results presented in text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because I6 is not met.

This study used resting-state seed-based functional connectivity in bipolar patients and did not include any task-based emotion regulation fMRI paradigm or visual emotional stimuli. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without a task activation map). Inclusion criterion I8 (sample: clinical participants) is met. However it fails to meet required inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I9 (within-task regulation/viewing contrast), and I10 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps). Full text appears complete and methods/results are provided, but the study does not address the meta-analysis objective of task-evoked emotion regulation to visual stimuli, so it must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional face stimuli with patient and control groups and reports within-task contrasts (emotional conflict adaptation) with coordinate results; however it does NOT meet key inclusion requirements. The meta-analysis requires an instructed emotion regulation task (I6), e.g., reappraise vs look; here regulation is implicit/non-instructed (the study explicitly tests spontaneous, non-instructed adaptation), so I6 is not met. Additionally, the paper reports results only within a priori ROIs with small-volume correction and displays findings within those ROIs (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation map reported), thus failing the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps with peak coordinates (I10). This violates exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI/SVC results reported). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (explicit ‘reality checking’/reappraisal) during anticipation and perception of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS). The paper reports within-task contrasts (exp negative > neutral; perc negative > neutral) and group comparisons, provides whole-brain, group-level analyses with cluster correction and refers to coordinate tables/supplementary material. The sample (patients with SAD, with cognitive-control and basic groups) is eligible, and the full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, within-group effects reported, and not an empathy/perspective-taking-only task). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI emotion regulation with visual stimuli.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual (video) stimuli with a clinical and control sample and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results. However, participants were not instructed to use any emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance); they simply watched clips and rated valence/arousal. Therefore the study does not meet inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: video clips), I8 (sample includes clinical and control groups), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts e.g., emotional>neutral), I10 (whole-brain group-level analyses), I11 (results clearly described in text/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed regulation). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI with visual emotional face distracters and reports within-task emotion contrasts and whole-brain exploratory results (in supplements), but it does NOT instruct participants to use an explicit emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli — faces), I8 (sample includes youth), I9 (reports within-task emotion-related contrasts: fear vs neutral effects), I10 (references whole-brain results/tables in supplement), I11 (coordinates/tables acceptable in supplement). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy — the task required performing an n-back with emotional distracters rather than an instructed reappraisal or other explicit regulation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Therefore, per instructions requiring ALL inclusion criteria to be satisfied, I exclude this study because I6 is not met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) and reports unregulated viewing contrasts (emotional valence > neutral) as well as whole-brain voxelwise group analyses with MNI coordinates. Sample includes patient and control groups reported separately. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given (i.e., I6 ‘instructed regulation’ is not present), the meta-analysis objective accepts studies that involve passive/unregulated viewing; the study therefore satisfies the required within-task unregulated contrast (I9). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empathy (intentional perspective-taking) fMRI study with visual face stimuli and whole-brain analyses. However, participants were instructed to empathize (share emotions), not to apply an emotion regulation strategy (no instructed reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other regulation), and the reported emotional contrasts reflect empathy versus baseline rather than an instructed regulation versus baseline/look contrast. This fits exclusion criterion E7 (empathy/perspective-taking with no instruction to amplify or dampen one's own emotional response). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I11 (whole-brain results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation contrast or a pure unregulated ‘view’ contrast distinct from an empathy instruction). Therefore the study should be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (increase/decrease) during presentation of visual IAPS photographs, reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. decrease > attend, increase > attend), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with Talairach peak coordinates and corrected clusters. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. All inclusion criteria are met (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) in an affective Stroop task, and reports unregulated viewing trials/contrasts (view negative/neutral/positive) linking BOLD responses to emotion (meets I9). Sample qualifies (trauma-exposed adults; I8). The study is task-based (I5) and uses visual stimuli (I7). The paper states that whole-brain results are reported in the Supplemental Results and reports voxelwise cluster results (facilitating meta-analysis), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I10/I11), despite primary ROI/SVC analyses. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not connectivity-only, not perspective-taking only, and whole-brain results are reported). Note: the task did not instruct an explicit emotion regulation strategy (I6 not applicable), but the review objective allows inclusion of unregulated viewing contrasts, which this paper provides.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal/downregulation (I6) of emotional responses to visual stimuli drawn from the IAPS (I7). Participants include clinical (bipolar I) and control groups with results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (decrease vs. observe) and unregulated viewing contrasts (observe negative vs. neutral) (I9). Group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with thresholding and anatomical labeling are reported (cluster Z>2.0, p=.05 corrected), satisfying whole-brain reporting with standard-space localization (I10), and results are clearly described in text and tables/figures (I11). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. The provided full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore INCLUDE.

This is a task-based fMRI study that presents visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures) and reports within-task contrasts (negative > neutral) as well as group-level whole-brain activation results. Participants include a clinical group (BPD) and healthy controls analyzed separately. Although the task did not instruct an emotion regulation strategy, the review accepts unregulated viewing contrasts (I9); therefore the study still meets the meta-analysis objective. The paper provides whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-level results with FDR correction) and ROI follow-ups, and reports sufficient methodological details and results for inclusion.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E4. The fMRI analyses reported are ROI-focused (DLPFC, BA24, BA25, amygdala) and partial-least-squares on selected regions; no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space are presented for emotion regulation contrasts. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I8 (clinical participant sample reported), I9 (reports within-task BOLD responses to negative-word trials/unregulated viewing contrasts). (c) Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal/distancing/acceptance—task involved emotion identification and digit-sorting, not instructed regulation), I7 (stimuli were words/sentences, not visual images or film/video), I10 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation map provided). Because the review requires instructed emotion-regulation tasks with visual stimuli and at least one whole-brain activation map, this study does not meet key criteria and should be excluded.

This task-based fMRI study (faces task) contrasts emotion labeling (an incidental/instructed form of emotion regulation) with emotion matching/gender labeling and reports within-task contrasts (e.g., emotion labeling vs emotion matching) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with thresholded Z-statistic images and peak coordinates. Stimuli are visual (faces). Sample includes adolescents and a control group reported separately. Thus it meets all relevant inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

The study must be excluded because it does not meet two required inclusion criteria. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5 met) with an eligible sample (I8 met), it reports within-task contrasts/un-modulated emotion contrasts (I9 met) and whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (I10, I11 met). However: (1) the fMRI task does NOT instruct an emotion regulation strategy—participants made likelihood judgments and were not asked to up- or down-regulate emotion (I6 NOT met); and (2) the emotional stimuli are textual descriptions/read events rather than visual emotional stimuli (images or film)—the methods indicate subjects “read different possible future events,” so stimuli are words/sentences which are excluded by I7 (I7 NOT met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met, failure to meet I6 and I7 requires exclusion.

The full text describes an empirical task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion regulation task (enhance/suppress/maintain) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). Within-task contrasts (positive suppress > positive maintain and negative suppress > negative maintain) are reported and used in hierarchical linear modeling to predict changes in anhedonia. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described with peak coordinates and cluster correction. The sample includes a clinical MDD group and a control group reported separately. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and should be INCLUDED.

While this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (faces) and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain/voxelwise results, it does not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses. Participants performed an emotion discrimination/classification task (threatening vs. not threatening) rather than an instructed regulation (e.g., reappraise, distance) during anticipation or stimulus presentation. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it is not a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation with whole-brain voxelwise results. Specifically: (a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 — the study reports only partial/region-limited coverage (fNIRS probe over LPFC) with no whole-brain analyses. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I7 (visual stimuli: computer-based frustration task), I8 (sample: children included), I9 (task-related contrasts: frustration > baseline task regressor reported). (c) Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not an fMRI study — uses fNIRS), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy; natural/spontaneous regulation was observed), I10 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps/standard-space peak coordinates). Because the meta-analysis requires fMRI whole-brain studies of instructed emotion regulation, this paper does not qualify.

This is a task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were instructed to use cognitive emotion-regulation strategies (attend vs regulate) during presentation of visual conditioned stimuli (colored squares). The paper reports within-task contrasts (CS+ vs CS−; regulate vs attend) and group-level voxelwise activation results identifying striatal and cortical regions (with supplementary tables/figures referenced for specific regions/values). The sample (n=15) is eligible and analyses include ROI extraction based on whole-brain contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided; supplementary tables are referenced but missing is acceptable per criteria.

This study is an MR spectroscopy (1H/31P-MRS) investigation at rest comparing personality disorder patients and healthy controls. It does not use task-based fMRI, does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy, and does not present visual emotional stimuli or report within-task regulation contrasts or whole-brain task activation maps. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using a sad mood elaboration paradigm that explicitly instructs participants to actively elaborate on an induced sad mood (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy; I6). The emotional stimuli are visual film clips (My Girl), which qualifies as visual stimuli (I7). The sample (children aged 7–11, including a clinical PO-MDD group and controls) meets the sample criterion (I8). The study reports within-task contrasts related to regulation/elaboration (elaboration > fixation baseline) and group comparisons (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps were computed and thresholded with coordinates reported (I10,I11). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical issues). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for the meta-analysis.

While this is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (paintings) with whole-brain group-level results and standard peak coordinates, it does not meet the review’s core requirement of an instructed emotion-regulation task. Specifically, no emotion-regulation strategy (e.g. reappraisal, distancing) was instructed during scanning (I6 not met), and the reported contrasts focus on sponsorship/valuation (sponsor > nonsponsor) rather than emotion-regulation contrasts or unregulated viewing of emotional stimuli (I9 not met). The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore, although I5, I7, I8, and I10 are satisfied, the absence of instructed regulation and of emotion-related regulation/viewing contrasts excludes the study from this meta-analysis.

Exclusion E4 applies: the paper reports task-based fMRI with visual stimuli and within-task (unregulated viewing) contrasts (I5, I7, I8, I9 satisfied) but does not provide a group-level whole-brain (unmasked) voxelwise task activation map or whole-brain peak coordinates. Analyses are reported using anatomical masks/ROIs (amygdala and prefrontal mask) and exploratory prefrontal-only voxelwise results; no unmasked whole-brain task-evoked statistical map is presented, hence it fails I10. Also, the task is passive viewing (no instructed emotion regulation), so I6 (instructed regulation) is not met. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation with visual (face) stimuli in children and reports unregulated viewing contrasts (sad > neutral), so it meets I5, I7, I8, and I9. However, it does not instruct participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal/other instructed regulation), so I6 is not met. Furthermore, the paper reports ROI/network-based analyses (predefined spherical ROIs and averaged network responses) rather than presenting a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates; therefore I10 is not met and Exclusion E4 (ROI-only results/no whole-brain analysis) applies. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs participants to deploy attention (attentional deployment) to arousing vs. non-arousing portions of unpleasant visual images (IAPS). The task constitutes an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (attentional deployment), stimuli are visual static images, and the sample is healthy adults. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g., unpleasant non-arousing focus > unpleasant arousing focus), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with peak activations (and coordinates in supplemental materials), and ROI analyses; full methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS/photos) and instructed appraisal tasks (self-referential processing and emotion labeling). The label condition is an instructed strategy that promotes detachment (an antecedent-focused/regulation-like manipulation) and the self condition modulates emotional engagement, fitting the review’s emotion-regulation vs. view comparisons. The paper reports within-task contrasts (self vs label; self/label vs control) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak MNI coordinates (tables/figures), satisfying reporting requirements. Full manuscript (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (only-ROI results, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or irrelevant perspective-taking) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I11 and should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (explicit emotion regulation: upregulate/downregulate) of visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Downregulate > View) and whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates in standard space (reported clusters and coordinates). Healthy control and patient groups are reported separately. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of implicit viewing of visual emotional stimuli (faces) with within-task contrasts (Emotion > Shape), so it meets I5, I7, I8, and I9. However the analyses focus on an ACC ROI (ACC123) and report only ROI-based voxelwise/statistical results within that mask (no reported whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space). Thus it violates exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI results reported). Inclusion criteria I6 (instructed emotion regulation) and I10 (whole-brain evidence) are not met. Full text appears complete. Excluded on the basis of E4.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs children to use guided cognitive reappraisal (decrease/increase) while viewing visual emotional images (IAPS/EmoPicS). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (negative-decrease vs. negative-attend; negative-attend vs. neutral-attend). The methods describe whole-brain voxelwise random-effects group analyses and report peak coordinates in MNI space (tables/ROIs and supplementary voxelwise results), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (Re-Interpret) for distressing visual stimuli (pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (ReappraiseDistressing > LookDistressing) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses (conjunction and PPI results), with activation clusters described in the text and supplementary materials. The sample (treatment-seeking adult smokers) is an eligible participant group. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; includes whole-brain task activation maps; not only connectivity; not only between-group contrasts; not an empathy/perspective-taking without regulation). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

Excluded because the regulated stimuli are script-driven verbal narratives (script-driven imagery/word/sentence stimuli), not visual stimuli; thus the study fails inclusion criterion I7. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive reappraisal task), I8 (sample reporting patient and control groups), I9 (within-task contrasts reported: UP>maintain, DOWN>maintain), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I11 (whole-brain results presented in tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED solely for not meeting I7 (non-visual, script-driven stimuli).

The study is a task-based fMRI with visual stimuli (peer face photographs) in adolescents, reports within-task contrasts (negative vs. positive feedback) and whole-brain results with peak coordinates. However, participants were not instructed to use any emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance); the task probed natural responses to social feedback rather than instructed regulation. Thus it fails inclusion criterion I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy). It meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11 but not I6, so it must be excluded per the review criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly tests instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal-style “suppress” and “enhance” instructions) while participants view visual stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (negative suppress vs. attend; positive enhance vs. attend) and performs voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses normalized to MNI space with reported peak coordinates and cluster correction. The sample (patients with MDD) is an eligible participant group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes within-task contrasts, not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation instructions). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: the fMRI task does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance); instead it uses an emotional Stroop/emotion conflict task that requires labeling emotion and ignoring an overlaid word (implicit attentional control), not explicit instructed regulation. Full text is complete. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli — faces), I8 (eligible sample: clinical and control groups reported separately), I9 (reports within-task contrast: incongruent > congruent emotional task contrast), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates), I11 (whole-brain results clearly described/figures and tables). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation). Because all inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I6 is not met, the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional face stimuli and an instructed regulation-like paradigm (redirecting attention during an emotional n-back), with appropriate within-task contrasts and a clinical at-risk sample (satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). However, all reported analyses are ROI-based (amygdala, ACC, PFC) and seed/ROI functional connectivity; the paper does not present any group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space. Thus it fails I10 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI/seed-based results with no whole-brain analysis). Full text appears complete. Consequently the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that used an emotion regulation paradigm (participants were cued to “look” or to reappraise), with visual stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports a within-task unregulated viewing contrast (look negative > look neutral) and whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with peak coordinates in standard space (MNI). Sample and analyses meet eligibility (adolescents; clinical and control data reported). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The human fMRI component used an emotional face go/no-go task that required attention/inhibition to emotional stimuli but did NOT instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance). Thus inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation) is not met. The study does satisfy I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports task-related responses to threat cues / unregulated viewing contrasts), and I11 (results presented in text/figures). Based on the provided full text there is no clear evidence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation map with peak coordinates reported in standard space (I10 not demonstrably met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are clearly triggered in the provided content. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails I6 (required) and does not demonstrably meet I10.

This task-based fMRI study (I5) of depressed and control participants (I8) reports within-task contrasts related to instructed memory control (F-NG > R-NG) (I9) and provides whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates (I10,I11). The fMRI task constitutes an instructed cognitive control manipulation (directed forgetting), so I6 is satisfied. However, the regulated stimuli are words (Chinese adjective words presented as verbal stimuli), not visual images or film clips; the review’s stimulus criterion excludes studies that regulate word/sentence stimuli. Therefore inclusion criterion I7 (visual emotional stimuli) is NOT met. No exclusion criteria from the review’s list (E3–E7) are triggered. Because I7 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual (movie) stimuli in children and adults and reports neural differences for unregulated viewing of positive/negative/neutral clips. However, it does not include any instructed emotion regulation task/strategy (violates I6). The paper reports multivariate classification results and region lists but does not provide a conventional group-level whole-brain task activation contrast with peak coordinates in standard space suitable for coordinate-based meta-analysis (violates I10 and thus I11). Therefore it fails to meet all required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli - film clips), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports unregulated viewing condition effects via within-task condition analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed regulation), I10 (no clearly reported whole-brain voxelwise peak coordinates/contrast maps), I11 (no qualifying coordinate tables/figures apparent). No exclusion criteria from the list apply.
